📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The countdown to Avengers: Doomsday is almost over. Years after Robert Downey Jr.'s return as Doctor Doom was announced on stage at San Diego Comic-Con, we're on the precipice of Doom's MCU debut, and to celebrate, we're taking a Stark Tech time machine back to 2018, when Total Film reported from the set of Avengers: Infinity War.

Pulled from the May 2018 glitch of Total Film magazine, this time capsule feature is a fascinating snapshot of the MCU ahead of its biggest (and arguably best) movie, with candid insight from Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Chadwick Boseman, Tom Holland, Elizabeth Olsen, the Russo brothers and many, many more.

Sources indicate that avengers: Doomsday is one of this year's (and any year's) most exciting upcoming movies, and there's no better time to revisit a crucial chapter on the road to Doomsday. When you're done reading this time capsule set report, be sure to check out our own experience revisiting the movie, as we consider why Avengers: Infinity War is "essential viewing" ahead of Avengers: Doomsday. But for now, let's take a trip to the set of Avengers: Infinity War….

In a recent development, pinewood Atlanta Studios, 2017. Total Film is on the top-secret set of Avengers: Infinity War, one of the few remaining instalments in the Marvel Cinematic Universe's Phase Three, and the culmination of the 18 previous MCU movies to date. It's the most ambitious team-up yet for a studio that pioneered the concept of assembling disparate heroes onscreen in an 'expanded universe'.

Recent findings suggest that at Chris 'Star-Lord' Pratt's estimate, there are 22 superheroes uniting to face down the ultimate major bad. What TF witnesses on Stage 9 is just a hint of the carnage that intergalactic villain Thanos (played by Josh Brolin, via motion-capture) will wreak when he comes to Earth to enact his grand strategy. Fire. Twisted metal. Fallen trees. Soil and gravel everywhere.

It has been revealed that crew members ensure that the fires are burning just where they need to be, as dozens of cast and stunt performers prepare to run purposefully out of a trench for a slow-motion shot. Details are scarce as to what's actually going on, but it's fair to assume something big has occurred. Avengers rub shoulders with Guardians, as Wakandan warriors take up arms alongside characters who look like they've stepped through a portal from another realm entirely.

Mark Ruffalo – in strategically spotted skin-tight pyjamas – has a mast attached to his head to indicate the Hulk's eyeline and the scale of his CGI avatar. By any measure – creative, logistical, and presumably budgetary – this is the biggest Marvel movie yet. Hydraulic canisters hiss, and bangs break out when action's called and the cameras roll.

It has been revealed that when we later catch up with the cast, snatching chats with handfuls of Avengers at a time, their bloodied and bruised faces attest to the trouble the superteam has found themselves in. But for now, the sheer scale of this diorama of destruction is jaw-dropping. "It's truly like herding cats," Captain America actor Chris Evans jokes to TF of the enormo-cast. "I look at the first AD, this poor guy. It's just hard to get everybody focused.".

During a break in filming, writers Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely (of all three Captain America movies) explain how they solved the challenge of incorporating so many heroes into one film: making genocidal Titan warlord Thanos the main character. Having been teased since the mid-credits sting of 2012's The Avengers, Thanos is finally taking his place in the sun.

"The thing that separates it from other Avengers movies for me is that the antagonist is the main character," notes McFeely. "So in many ways, this is Thanos's movie. It was the smartest way for us to accommodate all the characters and honour this [villain] that Marvel's been teasing for so long.".

In a recent development, when asked how high the stakes are, McFeely offers, "Is the universe high enough for you?" The Mad Titan has some high-minded ideals about how the universe should be, and his strategy involves wiping out about half of its inhabitants. In order to set his plan in motion, he needs six MacGuffins that have been seeded throughout the series so far: the Infinity Stones, which will slot into his golden gauntlet and give him godlike powers.

It has been revealed that "He wants six Infinity Stones," explains Markus. "And once you get them, you can do whatever you want." It goes some way towards explaining why quite such an exhaustive roster of heroes is required to even begin to fight off such an omnipotent foe and his "elite squad," the Black Order. But, following the events of Civil War, the divided superteam are at a low ebb.

"I mean, the whole point of doing Civil War was that they enter this movie fractured and separated, and that will play a very integral part of the film," explains Joe Russo, one half of the director duo, the Russo brothers. In Infinity War, the core Avengers – Iron Man, Cap, Thor, Black Widow, Hulk, et al. – will be joined by Black Panther, Spider-Man, Doctor Strange, the Guardians Of The frickin' Galaxy, and more.

In a recent development, so, after the head-to-head in Civil War, has the relationship between Iron Man and Cap improved at all? "I don't know that it could have gotten any worse," considers Evans when we catch him between takes, clad in his Cap suit, sans helmet and chest-piece, his face dirtied from the day's action. Robert Downey Jr. – the Iron Man star who was integral to kicking off the entire MCU – concurs.

Industry observers note that "I wouldn't say he does [get on with Cap]," Downey Jr. explains, holding court with the laid-back confidence of a talk show host. "I'm saying that because Thanos is the threat. I don't think it can be underestimated. It's not just what Josh Brolin is bringing to his portrayal of it, but there's something about it where we've all agreed that this is the sum of all of our fears. It's like Gestalt therapy at this point.".

Currently dressed in a camo T-shirt and hoodie, the (fake) blood above RDJ's eyebrow attests to a pretty physical form of therapy. "I think because the threat has risen to a newly introduced level – which is really saying something – that whether we want to band together or not, we won't survive unless we do," he continues. "So I think that's a bit of a new thing. So it's like, 'Can these disparate heroes get along after all?'".

Industry observers note that chris Hemsworth – out of his Thor costume and wearing a dressing gown over a black T-shirt and jogging bottoms – attests to the scale of the threat. "I think that [Thanos is] the strongest thing we've ever faced, his force," he indicates in his Aussie baritone. "And it brings out a whole other level of us, I think, and another stage or journey we need to embark on.".

Recent findings suggest that tom Holland strolls over to join Downey Jr. and Hemsworth. Munching on a banana to keep up his calorie intake, he's clad in black mo-cap pyjamas (a requirement of his upgraded Spider-Man suit), with a puffer jacket to keep him warm in the empty neighbouring soundstage we're now occupying, and he's sporting a bloodied nose.

Recent findings suggest that keen to avoid dropping spoilers (as he's been known to do on social media), Holland's staying tight-lipped about Peter Parker's journey, although he does tease that "he matures a lot", before Downey Jr. adds with a sly grin: "Things you wouldn't expect are endured.".

It has been revealed that dishing out the cuts and bruises is Thanos, who'll draw all the other characters into his orbit. Having a bad guy at the forefront will mark a real change of pace for the typically hero-heavy MCU, and means that Thanos needs the requisite depth to carry the film.

"We were considering showing his backstory," says Anthony Russo, "but ultimately felt it wasn't necessary for the movie. However, the movie is told from his point of view. I think it's a very interesting space for an audience to be in, because every villain thinks they're the hero of their own story. We thought it'd become compelling to track a villain's point of view through a movie.".

In a recent development, anthony Russo goes on to call Brolin's performance "stunning", explaining that he brings "an intensity and a violence, but also at the same time, a charm and a sensitivity. It's a very complicated character. He's at times despicable and horrifying, and at other times oddly empathetic.".

Because the threat has risen to a new level, whether we want to band together or not, we won't survive unless we do.

Industry observers note that having Brolin on set (albeit in those unavoidable mo-cap pyjamas) gives the digital character added heft, as well as providing the actors with something to work against. "It really is mind-blowing how sensitive a performance we can translate into a CG character now, and how much of Josh's performance is in that character," adds Joe Russo.

"He brings some humanity to something that could just be a one-dimensional villain," claims Karen Gillan, her friendly Scottish accent bizarrely contrasting with the menacing blue makeup she's covered in to play Gamora. "I can't look him in the eye, but I hear his voice," says Black Panther star Chadwick Boseman of working opposite Brolin when he's mo-capping an eight-foot-tall character. "He's right there.".

Yes, Black Panther and his Wakandan allies will play a crucial part in Infinity War, with the third-act battle set to go down on his home turf. Given the astonishing success of T'Challa's recent solo movie, his presence will only heighten the anticipation for Infinity War. "Being able to bring that energy into Infinity War, and that dimensionality and those themes into our movie, it's a gift for us," beams Joe Russo.

When we speak to Boseman on set, he looks like one cool cat in his full Panther get-up (minus the mask), even with a long coat draped over his shoulders.

"How does he fit in as an Avenger?" Boseman considers. "I don't know if it's a situation where it's like a club that you join. I think the fact that Wakanda, to a certain degree, opens up a fresh place for the Avengers to fit. As opposed to him fitting into the Avengers, he opens up a new space. And that's pretty much all I can say." That charismatic chuckle booms. "That's all I can say!".

Sources indicate that boseman is just one of several newly successful solo characters who'll be joining the Avengers lineup. "It's like Voltron, you know what I mean?" quips Evans of the characters uniting. "This other franchise starts doing well, and they start forming one giant thing. It's really exciting.".

Avengers: Infinity War 5* review: "Bold, ballsy, satisfying, and dramatic".

Benedict Cumberbatch's Doctor Strange will also play a key role, being brought into the fold with Wong (Benedict Wong) via Tony Stark and Bruce Banner/Hulk (Ruffalo). Holland's Spidey also returns after high-school spin Homecoming. "I would have been first in line to see The Avengers, so to be on an Avengers film set as a 21-year-old is surreal," Holland enthuses, grinning like, well, a 21-year-old on an Avengers film set.

In a recent development, hemsworth, mock-disgruntled, chips in: "What makes me laugh about this whole thing is, it was not too long ago that [I was being asked]: 'What's it like to be the fresh one?' I'm like, 'Oh my God, I'm getting really old.' I'm the past now. This is the future. It's the transition." Hot on the heels of Thor: Ragnarok, the gut-bustingly funny threequel that saw Thor and Hulk flexing their comedic muscles, that duo will find themselves in a slightly more serious predicament this time out.

According to recent reports, "God knows I tried [to be funny]," laughs Ruffalo, his face still dotted with mo-cap markers. "It's the Russo brothers, so it's not quite as comedic. Of course, we're fighting Thanos, and that's not funny. But we tried to keep some of that spontaneous combustion alive. Banner's very, very different in this movie. They're all really different. I feel like I've been lucky. I got to do this character in steps, and I have had a plotted-out arc of how this character's developed and changed over all these movies. So you're going to see another surprising incarnation of Banner.".

Also returning, and last seen in Civil War, is Elizabeth Olsen's Scarlet Witch. Her fledgling relationship with Vision (Paul Bettany) was hinted at in that film, and will be explored further here. "It was a lot of fun for Paul and me," claims Olsen, her character's fingerless gloves peeking out from the sleeves of her black coat. "I think we didn't know if we were going to, I guess, scratch that itch of those characters and their relationship. So we've kind of layered it in since [Avengers: Age Of] Ultron. Now we actually got to fulfil that throughline, which was actually really cool, to have something to really anchor us to the film.".

Although the fact that Vision's forehead bears one of the Infinity Stones that Thanos wants might impact their courtship. As well as putting existing relationships under stress, having this many heroes on screen throws up opportunities for unexpected character-combos. "That's one of the fun things that's going to happen in these two movies, those introductions of those characters to each other," notes Don 'War Machine' Cheadle, sporting the unofficial uniform of, yep, mo-cap PJs. "Everyone's kind of like, 'Who is this dude? I don't know why you guys are even here!' We get to throw them all together and see how they respond to each other.".

Industry observers note that of course, franchise stalwart Black Widow (Scarlett Johansson) returns, as does former Winter Soldier Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan), Falcon (Anthony Mackie) and Hawkeye (Jeremy Renner), who has been seen sporting a latest mohawk but has been absent from all trailers so far. "All will be explained when people see the movie," teases Anthony Russo of Hawkeye's absence. "It's all tied into the story.".

It has been revealed that although the one group of characters who could really shake things up are the Guardians Of The Galaxy, the ragtag team of spacefarers who have little regard for traditional heroics, and strut to their own mixtape beat. From the first trailer, when Thor spies the bunch of a-holes and asks, "Who the hell are you guys?", the chemistry seemed inevitable.

That moment is Downey Jr.'s favourite of the whole film: "I'm like, 'Sold!' If the whole third movie was that scene, we're fine, because the Guardians are also just a whole other wackadoo, awesome, super-creative integer." When we talk to Star-Lord himself, Chris Pratt, he's wearing his signature red leather jacket and also has a dirtied, bloody face.

"The stakes have never been higher," he states between forkfuls of lunch from a Tupperware pot (the cast and crew are working 'French hours' and eating on the fly). "All the movies have led towards this. You couldn't just have any old standard villain. You have to have the one villain who touched every one of those characters' storylines.".

Sources indicate that "Well, I sensed glory, but I will tell you this: I just have such pride. Really, honestly, the main thing is, I think we really have become this oddball family that genuinely looks after and cares for each other, and supports each other. So that's a first for me. The other thing is, none of us would be here at this stage without Joss [Whedon]. Because he did a proof-of-concept execution that was monumental. But then there's been a quantum – literally – shift in the way that things are going now, where all these different franchises are on the horizon, and they're bringing new energy, and some of us are maybe tapping out or going away. Who knows what the future is? But the task is yet to be completed. I don't think I've been hoisted up in a chair and marched around yet like I deserve, but we'll see.".

Asked if he's changed his approach to playing Peter Quill after jumping from the relatively MCU-isolated Guardians movies to this multi-character sandbox, Pratt responds, "I guess a little bit. We get to bring some of the Guardians' flavor to this movie, which is nice. You get to be a little more vibrant, a little more irreverent, a little more colourful. So you're not carrying the dramatic weight or anything like that.".

According to recent reports, on how the Avengers experience compares to Guardians, Pom 'Mantis' Klementieff gasps, "It's major..." GOTG Vol.2's scene-pinching empath right now has two small antennae sprouting from her head that'll be boosted in post-production. "There are so many people, and so many incredible actors. The Guardians set felt more like a family because we all know each other. But [here] we start knowing more about the others, and then we're going to wrap...".

Speaking of family, there's another reason the Guardians will be significant for Infinity War: both Nebula and Gamora (Zoe Saldana) were raised as Thanos' 'daughters', before breaking away. "What can I say?" grins Karen Gillan. "This is where I get nervous because I'm going to give away spoilers. It's definitely going to be explored further. Her relationship with Gamora is going to get really interesting because of a certain element that I can't tell you...".

Industry observers note that "I don't even know what you're talking about," cuts in Olsen (most actors didn't get a complete script). "Oh, it's so good," laughs Gillan in response. "It's so good. It's going to be great." Chris Evans was one of the few to get a complete script. "I luckily was able to get a script," smiles Evans. "The majority of people on set are like, 'So what are we doing today?' The Russos have to give a loose description of what's happening. I didn't complain. I was just like, 'Give me a fucking script! Give me a script. I need to know what's going on!'".

Industry observers note that what could make Infinity War (and Avengers: Endgame ) so monumental is that it arrives at the time when the MCU is welcoming a lot of fresh blood, while older contracts might be coming to an end. This could be a time of metamorphosis and reinvigoration. Naturally, cast and crew avoid spoilers, but they do promise that the roster is in for a shake-up, and we could see some permanent exits.

"We have not had any special death requests," indicates McFeely, but co-writer Markus says that Marvel was open to anything, and they had free rein to kill off whomever the story dictated should go. "You don't want to… I'm talking around things," stutters Markus. "You don't want to cut off a flower just as it's beginning to bloom… But a nice big flower maybe you could.".

"It's one of the reasons these movies can be special, because Kevin [Feige, Marvel Studios president] and the rest of Marvel allow us big swings, right?" adds McFeely. "There wasn't a mandate that everything has to get tied up so that we can continue with another one. I feel these movies are most successful when the characters undergo big changes, and – in our case – when someone is escorted off the stage. So that allows for some really good storytelling.".

In a recent development, "It's a cocktail of emotions," states Evans of this beginning of the end of a particular era of the MCU. "It's nice because it really has evolved the way you would hope." For all the talk of death, the atmosphere on set isn't morose, and the camaraderie of the cast is evident. After all, they've had enough films to forge a bond on, and they're clearly enjoying being part of such an expansive repertory.

I didn't complain. I was just like, 'Give me a fucking script! Give me a script. I need to know what's going on!'.

"I've never felt like a fan as much as I have on these films," grins Hemsworth. "Like meeting [the Guardians] as Thor, but also as Chris, was equally as exciting and upcoming, and it brought in a whole different energy. Especially these last few days, we've had just about every member of the Marvel Universe on the set.".

According to recent reports, "It's been the Ben-Hur of the MCU, for sure," chimes Downey Jr. Now, the gang are looking ahead to Avengers: Endgame, which arrives in 2019, and was shot back-to-back with Infinity War. When we catch up with the Russos again in March 2018, they've "locked" picture on Infinity War and are in the final stages of tweaking VFX and sound, and they once again assure that Infinity War and Endgame will be two very separate films (rather than being 'half' a movie each).

"We're very, very happy with it, and we're very excited with where the story goes," notes Joe Russo. "I think it's going to be really surprising to audiences. We're excited for the anticipation that that will create for Avengers: Endgame. They're very distinctly different movies. I think that people will be pleased with the fact that they get different styles and tones in both films, and different narratives."'.

In a recent development, the cast and filmmakers couldn't be more excited about how fans are going to react to the two upcoming movies (which will have Ant-Man and the Wasp and Captain Marvel sandwiched between them). "It's going to be messy," Ruffalo states of the audience reaction. "There's going to be a lot of messes in the theater. Heads exploded… People pooping their pants.".

"I wasn't going to say that, but you're right," laughs Boseman. "This one, it does have that sense of a finale," adds Pratt. "Have you ever seen a great fireworks show, and you're like, 'How the fuck did they do that?' It gives you goosebumps. That's this movie. That's this combination of movies.".

"Yeah," admits Pratt, "It's true.".

Tech Report: Remembering the back alley brawls of The Warriors, a Rockstar city game that isn't an open world

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (942 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The older I get, the more fascinated I somehow become by how videogames depict night, how particular technologies at particular times give rise to particular nightlives.
  • In a recent development, probably the best move Rockstar made with their adaptation of Walter Hill's film is to retain the element of phantasmagoria.
  • Sources indicate that there's a lot of demand right now for a PC version of GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The older I get, the more fascinated I somehow become by how videogames depict night, how particular technologies at particular times give rise to particular nightlives. I've already gushed about the Starlight Zone in Sonic the Hedgehog – the mild dissociation incubated by the soft, ceaseless glare of the construction yard, the eyeless brick at the level's nadir, the sleepless glitter of the skyline. Now, let me wind the clock forward, and backward, to Rockstar Toronto's The Warriors. One long night from the late '70s, sweaty and electric and menacing, fed through dank and sullen polygons from 2005.

In a recent development, probably the best move Rockstar made with their adaptation of Walter Hill's film is to retain the element of phantasmagoria. Both the game and the movie open with a view of Coney Island's Wonder Wheel, its neon lamps forming a floating tracery of Morse code, cabins swinging almost imperceptibly against solid darkness. This is a kind of night in which light is more emblem than illumination, refusing to travel far, clinging to its source like a frightened ghost.

Sources indicate that there's a lot of demand right now for a PC version of GTA 6. I'd love a proper PC port of The Warriors, first, and not just because I like coming up with fancy ways to talk about Ferris wheels. A PC port would be a timely reminder that Rockstar used to make city games that aren't open worlds, city games made of levels, and were pretty good at it. The classic thrill of GTA is to jump into a car and circle the metropolis, radio on and arm dangling, snatches of pedestrian dialogue bursting in your wake as you zip through downtown, the skyscrapers streaming by and evaporating, the world your oyster. In The Warriors, the city is No Man's Land and the night is a tightly compartmentalised maze. Your goal is to reach the other side of it on your own two feet, before a thousand rival miscreants kick your head in.

Sources indicate that you lead a group of angry young guys of different ethnicities, wearing tribal colours and following a martial code - spiritual descendants of the stranded Greek soldiers of Xenephon's Anabais. Women barely feature in this relentlessly macho fable, and are mostly depicted as victims or seducers. Other genders are totally absent, while gay characters were considered for the film, but eventually cut. The game expands the storyline, filling in events before the titular Coney Island tearaways find themselves framed for a murder during an attempted city-wide gang uprising. But it otherwise adheres religiously to the movie's dingy and hyperbolic direction, hugging the visual language in ways that are slightly odd to return to, now that Rockstar have arguably outgrown their nerdy inferiority complex before the giants of cinema.

The game's Fresh York is mysterious and sparsely populated: the only people abroad are other gangs and cops. The playable areas eschew affluent districts and pleasure zones; instead, you hop over a million chainlink fences in subway terminals and trashy alleyways. Most of the buildings are sealed and silent. The sky is a painted forest of chimneys, silos and stripped low cloud. You keep waiting for Batman to descend from the girders of a flyover; some of the enemy gangs certainly wouldn't look out of place in Rocksteady's Arkham. The murk isn't quite as pungent as you'd find in a PS1 flâneur like Urban Chaos, but it's respectably enveloping. I'd linger here, a plummy-accented tourist with a headful of references, cooing decorously over the stained and withdrawn shopfronts, were it not for the constant risk of getting stomped.

In a recent development, back in the day, a few reviewers described The Warriors as having "deep" combat, offering a selection of directional jabs and kicks, grappling moves, terrain finishers and squad commands. I can't really see it. Certainly, The Warriors is no Sleeping Dogs. What the Warriors is is a believably chaotic brawler, with an enjoyable taste for friendly fire.

In a recent development, you spot a couple other Warriors surrounded by face-painted Baseball Furies, and launch into a crossbody tackle that bowls the whole group over. You straddle one of the clowns and are about to punch his teeth out when a friend lobs a trash can at the both of you. Now black-eyed and bleeding, you seize a dropped bat and swing randomly into the mob of warring outfits. Insults, taunts, chair legs and beer bottles fly back and forth. It feels like a fight. The riot spills out over each map, onto rooftops and into any businesses that have unwisely decided to stay open late. Looking back, I can see the first inklings of those spectacular drunken bar scuffles in Red Dead Redemption 2, though nobody's packing heat. The almost total absence of guns is, of course, the other thing that makes The Warriors novel, if you come to it from GTA.

It has been revealed that I've yet to play Rockstar's latest GTA, which is now available on console worldwide. I've yet to decide how it fits into my evolving half-arsed anthropology of videogame nightlife. Still, I've spent a fair amount of time looking at screenshots and videos, and I'm finding the nights too bright. Too bright! All those shades seeping everywhere, all those rays being traced, all the spotlights and sequins, the way everything glimmers or glistens – it's too heady for me. Send me back to 2005's Newly introduced York, where the darkness feels like it's part of the very mortar, and there's always a friend willing to "accidentally" hurl a bin at my head.

PlayStation defeats £2 billion UK lawsuit that alleged Sony forced consumers into "excessive and unfair prices"

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (484 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness).
  • The case, brought by Alex Neill, who mentioned she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store.
  • "Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value users who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness). The judgment came after a 30-day Competition Appeal Tribunal that took place in London, where PlayStation customers claimed Sony had removed "all actual and potential competition" in relation to selling digital games on the console.

The case, brought by Alex Neill, who mentioned she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store. In a judgment published by the London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal today (17th November), the case was rejected. The judgement noted that market definitions used to define Sony's conduct were "unsafe", and that consumers "would be likely to make informed choices when purchasing consoles" and games on the hardware, too.

"Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value users who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.

According to recent reports, the lawsuit made the argument that, upon purchasing a PS5 or other PlayStation console, you were then trapped within its ecosystem, and forced into paying the prices determined by Sony. The Tribunal disagreed, however, and ruled that Sony competed within a wider 'systems market' alongside Xbox, Nintendo and PC, for example. Furthermore, the Tribunal found no evidence that the existence of other digital storefronts would have actually brought any PlayStation Store pricing down.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, the Tribunal used the argument that consumers can also opt and buy physical games instead of using the PlayStation Store - something that is changing as of the start of 2028. That did not seem to have any bearing on today's decision, though. It's also worth noting that this case did not seek to interrogate the ownership status of digital games - something that's been at the heart of the movement rallying against Sony's decision to kill off physical media. Earlier this year, spokespeople from Sony's legal team argued "reasonable consumers" already know they don't actually own their digital games.

The London Tribunal has a fairly long history. Back in 2022, it began as a case that attempted to sue Sony to the tune of £5bn for "ripping people off" on PlayStation Store. Sony argued the case brought against it in this trial was "flawed from start to finish". This isn't the only situation where we're seeing consumers pursue legal action against the platform holder. Last year, PlayStation was sued in the Netherlands over the so-called "Sony tax" that highlighted artificially inflated prices on the Store, and sought to represent more than 20,000 participants that felt short-changed by the company.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • There were some minor scattered instances of PSN outages on Wednesday evening prior to the Rockstar title’s big launch, but these never affected everyone and the network recovered pretty fast.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We’d rightly criticise Sony if the PS5 had fallen to pieces during GTA 6’s launch, so let’s give the platform holder a nod of approval for navigating these past two weeks almost flawlessly.

There were some minor scattered instances of PSN outages on Wednesday evening prior to the Rockstar title’s big launch, but these never affected everyone and the network recovered pretty fast. I think we can give that a pass.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, the preload process worked flawlessly as far as I’m aware. I haven’t really seen any widespread reporting of people being unable to download the game in advance of its release.

Given its size and the sheer number of people wanting to play – remember, 32.5 million copies were sold across all consoles prior to release – that’s a humongous strain on Sony’s servers, which is predicted to have accounted for approximately 75% of all purchases.

Obviously GTA 6 is a single player-only game, so that certainly put less stress on the PSN as a whole, and the upcoming GTA Online’s eventual launch will be an even bigger test – but for now, the PS5 has held up remarkably well.

I’m not saying we should get out the champagne – this is the experience consumers quite rightly expect Sony to deliver.

Sources indicate that following a family tragedy, Sara and her son, Tom, seek a fresh start at Jagged Shore Cliff, but it swiftly unravels into a new nightmare. In their new and mysterious home, a dusty cabinet holds Baptiste, an unsettling doll accompanied by an ominous warning: “Never release this from its glass prison.” What ought to have been a shelter becomes the scene of a nightmare that defies all logic, putting their sanity and desire to survive to the test.

Rather than rely on jump scares, Baptiste‘s take on the psychological horror genre combines atmospheric tension and emotional depth, exploring how tragedy and loss can fracture a family’s reality, particularly through the lens of a child attempting to cope with intensely traumatic events. It also examines the descent into madness, blurring the lines between what is real and what is a nightmare, reflecting the fragile state of the mind under extreme emotional distress to tell a story of human vulnerability.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Online marketplace Etsy, best known as a platform for selling handmade goods, recently updated its user agreement to allow itself to "develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies" using content uploaded by sellers.

Sources indicate that this has not gone over well, with some closing their Etsy shops in protest. In response, Etsy has assured consumers that it doesn't plan to train AI systems designed to copy their work or replace their creativity. Instead, the organization said that the change is about improving the platform and providing "services and tools that can help you run your business.".

According to recent reports, I am sometimes sympathetic toward companies that get yelled at for normal terms of service agreements. If a manufacturer hosts user-submitted content on the web, for instance, it needs a license to distribute that content globally, and sometimes users misunderstand that. This is not one of those cases.

The latest agreement—which Etsy has told The New York Times it's planning to revise—says that Etsy and its third-party partners have the right to use uploaded content "to develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies, including to improve the Services and/or help keep them safe.".

That reads to me like blanket permission to train AI on user content for any purpose. The tacked-on note about keeping users safe does nothing to limit what Etsy can do.

The artists who sell cool custom keycaps and other fun things on Etsy are already likely to struggle against knock-off sellers if they get popular enough. That came with the territory of online selling even before AI, but it is absurd to now insist that they willingly hand over all the things that make their stores unique—their art, their product descriptions—to systems capable of duplicating those things in hard-to-trace ways, with only a pinky swear to protect them.

Recent findings suggest that we've all seen how the AI industry has tried to brush off the concerns of artists and others whose work it ingests. One firm went so far as to create a chatbot bearing the name of a former PC Gamer editor without permission, pretending that this robo-editor could give writing advice like the real person. And that's without him even knowing they were doing it!

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Even if Etsy truly does have good intentions, expecting artists to give this the thumbs up is ridiculous. It is not their responsibility to improve the platform by letting it mimic their creative work. The revised terms should, at the very least, exclude every seller from AI training as the default setting.

#86087. The Unexpected History of 'Black Friday'

The Unexpected History of 'Black Friday'

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1206 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, since the 1950s, Black Friday—once simply known as "the day after Thanksgiving"—has grown into a quasi-holiday in the United States marked by steep discounts, ceaseless shopping, and occasional violence.
  • While pre-dawn trips to the mall are waning as online shopping grows, in-person shopping on Black Friday is still a significant deal in the U.S.—it’s estimated that around 80 million Americans visited a brick-and-mortar store on Black Friday in 2025.
  • Industry observers note that “Black Friday” in the United States originally referred to the start of the Panic of 1869, when the collapse of the price of gold devastated the national economy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, since the 1950s, Black Friday—once simply known as "the day after Thanksgiving"—has grown into a quasi-holiday in the United States marked by steep discounts, ceaseless shopping, and occasional violence. But more recently, Black Friday has also metastasized. It's not a day anymore. It's a week, a month, a veritable state of mind. (Speaking of which, check out Lifehacker's Black Friday coverage. We got all the deals, baby!).

While pre-dawn trips to the mall are waning as online shopping grows, in-person shopping on Black Friday is still a significant deal in the U.S.—it’s estimated that around 80 million Americans visited a brick-and-mortar store on Black Friday in 2025. But how did Black Friday come about, and what does it all mean?

Industry observers note that “Black Friday” in the United States originally referred to the start of the Panic of 1869, when the collapse of the price of gold devastated the national economy. “Black Friday” as a description of the day after Thanksgiving dates back to 1951; the term first appeared in the journal Factory Management and Maintenance, where it referred to the number of employees who skipped work on the day after Thanksgiving. Around the same time, the police in Philadelphia and Rochester started informally using “Black Friday” to describe the traffic and crowds that appeared in their cities as shoppers hit the stores on the day after Thanksgiving. The phrase gradually caught on. It was picked up by national press in 1975 when the New York Times used "Black Friday" specifically to describe the day after Thanksgiving and the shopping and sales it brings.

But even before it had a name, Black Friday was a thing. The day after Thanksgiving has been known by merchants as the start of the shopping season since the late 1800s. By the early 20th century, retailers sponsored Thanksgiving Day parades that traditionally ended with an appearance by Santa Claus, as if to say, “Now it’s time to shop for Christmas.” By unspoken agreement among retailers, Christmas-themed advertisements rarely appeared before Thanksgiving in our grandparents’ day. This informal bargain obviously no longer applies.

Referring to a day as “black” traditionally denotes a period of calamity or tragedy, leading some to suggest different names for the day. In the early 1960s, Philadelphia merchants suggested “Substantial Friday,” a name which did not catch on, leaving retailers with the weak explanation that the “black” in Black Friday refers to the black ink denoting profits in a ledger. Oft-repeated lore suggests that retailers are "in the red" all year, and only start making an annual profit at the end of the year, but big retail chains generally make money all year long.

A more modern issue with the name is that Black Friday sales now last for days or even weeks, beginning in early to mid-November and bleeding over into the following Saturday, Sunday, “Cyber Monday,” Tuesday, and beyond, leading people to say things like, “Do you want to go Black Friday shopping this Sunday?” So far, alternative names like “Five-Day Frenzy” and “The day I get to trample someone to save $8 on a Nespresso” haven’t caught on. But here’s hoping.

Beginning around 2010, an insatiable thirst for profits led many retailers to push the start of Black Friday shopping to Thursday (aka Thanksgiving Day). Kmart opened Thanksgiving morning. Toys R Us opened that night. By 2011, Walmart was opening its doors at 10 p.m. on Thursday. The trend led to widespread backlash, with many Americans appalled that employees were forced to work on Thanksgiving or angry that consumerism was encroaching upon a holiday meant to celebrate colonialism. By 2021, most major retailers had relented and elected to remain closed on Thanksgiving.

It has been revealed that the term “Cyber Monday” describes the boost in online retail sales on the Monday after Thanksgiving, sparked by workers returning to the office and getting right to online shopping. The term first appeared on Nov. 28, 2005, in a Shop.org press release entitled “'Cyber Monday’ Promptly Becoming One of the Biggest Online Shopping Days of the Year," which may be the most influential press release ever written. Since its early 2000s birth, Cyber Monday has become the biggest online shopping day of the year. Americans spent $14.25 billion online on Cyber Monday 2025, according to Adobe Analytics. So is Cyber Monday bigger than Black Friday? Retailers really don't care: Analysts now tend to mash everything into the category of "Black Friday–Cyber Monday" (or even "Cyber Week").

If all this naked consumerism makes you a little squeamish, you're not alone. Anti-consumerists have named the day after Thanksgiving “Buy Nothing Day,” which you can celebrate by doing charity work, cutting up your credit cards, or simply not purchasing anything. Pioneered by artist Ted Dave and popularized by Adbusters magazine, the first Buy Nothing Day was celebrated in Canada in 1992.

In a recent development, it’s hard to measure the success of the alternative holiday. Both online and brick-and-mortar retail sales have increased sharply since 1992, suggesting Buy Nothing Day’s effect is negligible. On the other hand, maybe major retailers are losing millions because someone on Bluesky reminded you not to shop. Sure.

Industry observers note that depending on how you measure it, Black Friday has resulted in between one and 17 deaths. Jdimytai Damour is the only person killed directly due to a Black Friday sale: The 34-year-old worker was trampled to death by a surging crowd at a Long Island Walmart on Black Friday in 2008. If you include car accidents, shootings, retail worker suicides, and fatal heart attacks, Black Friday’s death toll balloons to 17, with 128 reported injuries.

Black Friday violence has even inspired a horror flick: Eli Roth's 2023 holiday-themed slasher Thanksgiving opens with a hilariously brutal Black Friday riot at a significant box store, setting off a chain of events that involve a lot of people being murdered by a dude in a Pilgrim mask.

I mean, yeah, of course. Critics of Black Friday point out that there are arguably better times to buy a upcoming TV (like the week before the Super Bowl), not to mention plenty of other goods. Savings from Black Friday shopping are often illusory—big-ticket “doorbuster” items generally sell out swiftly, leaving behind goods that are, by and large, priced the same as they would be at any other time of year. Some retailers even mark up products ahead of Black Friday so the discounts look bigger. If you're buying online, your browser history, location, and cart contents can tweak the prices you see on Black Friday, as they can on any other day.

Yet despite protest holidays, the unpleasantness of shopping when stores are overcrowded, and the frustration of hunting for bargains that often aren't that great to begin with, Black Friday stubbornly remains an unofficial holiday, celebrated by over 100 million Americans in one way or another. What that says about our country's relationship with capitalism is unclear, but personally, I’m going to continue my own day-after-Thanksgiving tradition of eating pie for breakfast and thinking about going for a walk, but then watching The Quick and the Dead instead. I'm not protesting anything; I just don't need the hassle.

According to recent reports, last night, I reported that GTA 6’s Metacritic user score was racking up ‘0’ review scores at an unprecedented pace. Many of the ratings were bogus.

In the hours since, the Switch 2’s universally adored remake of Ocarina of Time has seen its user score drop from 9.6 to 8.9 at the time of writing.

One ‘0’ rating simply reads: “Take your own medicine.”.

At this point, I just wish Metacritic would do away with user scores, although I’ve no doubt this sorry situation is all good for business.

Recent findings suggest that the thing is: this isn’t the first time the critic aggregator has become a battleground like this. As I mentioned in my original report, many of the greatest games ever made have pitiful user scores on the site.

Hopefully this all blows over, because it’s all rather embarrassing right now.

Original Story: GTA 6, the highest-rated game of all-time, is getting review bombed on Metacritic as idiots attempt to plunge the seminal Rockstar release’s rating with bogus ‘0’ scores.

At the time of writing, the title has a user score of 5.4, meaning it’s considered ‘Mixed or Average’:.

This is in sharp contrast to critics, who awarded the game an average score of 99, making it the best-reviewed title of all time.

“Good thing Rockstar doesn’t blacklist user ratings like they do critics,” one review reads.

There’s a theory among some online that the dev blacklists media outlets for giving its games poor scores, but it put GTA 6 in the hands of more than 150 critics, so I don’t buy that for a single second.

According to recent reports, many of the ‘0’ reviews all touch on the same thing: 30fps is “unplayable”, the series has gone “woke”, and the “story is horrible”. (“I never smiled one time,” writes one seemingly perpetually miserable user.).

Sources indicate that there are some legitimate criticisms among these; one person writes they’re not a fan of the life sim elements and prefer the “power fantasy” of older games. That’s fair, but it doesn’t make it a ‘0’.

Metacritic reviews have always been a disaster really, because you don’t need to actually own a game to rate it. Many of the best titles ever released have dreadful user scores on the site.

On the PS Store, though – where you actually have to spend money on the game to score it – the current rating sits at 4.84 based on 170k reviews. So that’s probably a better reflection of how the community feels.

My take on all this is that humans are predictable creatures: wherever there’s something popular, you’re probably going to find a group of people eager to tear it down.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft have laid off 166 developers, with this latest round of cuts at the Assassin's Creed and Far Cry publishers taking place at two of their studios in Eastern Canada. Both studios affected, Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, had a hand in last year's Assassin's Creed Shadows, with Montreal especially being a major and long-tenured development hub for the manufacturer.

Both IGN and GamesIndustry.biz report that the cuts, which amount to just under 4% studios' total combined headcount, affected staff working on recently cancelled or significantly changed projects.

"Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations," Ubisoft mentioned in a statement handed to both sites. "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

Ubisoft Montreal are currently working on Assassin’s Creed Hexe, reportedly a witchy tale set during the time of the Holy Roman Empire, which switched creative directors earlier this ear and is one of the games Ubi are keen to get out of the door. What Quebec have been up to since Shadows shipped is less clear. They're a much smaller than Montreal and were founded in 2005.

Ubisoft have been carrying out mass cuts across their studios worldwide all the way through this year. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx. Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona. Long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm. Ubisoft's Paris HQ. Three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz. All have been subjected to some form of cuts or closure.

Sources indicate that meanwhile. changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Solidarity to all of the Ubisoft workers who've been affected by these layoffs in Montreal and Quebec.

The Sniper of La Perle, Kodak Black's 22-track playlist, becomes available as soon as you scan four posters around La Perle at TWA Ponya Tattoo, Drip Drops, Aunt Zola's Soul Food, and the Jack of Hearts nightclub. The shops automatically marked themselves on my map as I drove around La Perle and Crosstown, but I've included screenshots highlighting their specific locations in Vice City's Haitian district. Once you arrive at one, Jason or Lucia's phone should alert you to something nearby you can scan with a notification from the Waink It app.

Look right as soon as you enter the parlor. There's a Sniper of Perle poster on the small table by the door.

You'll find another Sniper of Perle poster lying on the cash register counter.

The Sniper of Perle poster is immediately to the left as you enter, on a corkboard in front of the cash register.

It has been revealed that head upstairs to the second floor and enter the Jack of Hearts recording studio. Pass through the lobby and into the control room, then you'll see the Sniper of Perle poster lying on the table beside a fan.

In a recent development, once you arrive at the nightclub, head through the entrance corridor and look at the back wall. The poster is right there, and one quick scan is all it takes to unlock The Vault's playlist.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games has laid off around 60 people.

It has been revealed that the cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter. Studio head Heather Hazen is also leaving.

Its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer". The project will continue, but "may face a shakeup as a result of the cuts".

A spokesperson for 2K, the Take-Two label that runs Firaxis, confirmed Hazen's departure to Bloomberg, and said the studio is "restructuring and recentering around the studio's core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years".

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis," the spokesperson continued. "These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.".

The layoffs come two days before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, which is developed and published by Rockstar, a separate label at Take-Two.

In September, around 18 months after Civ 7's widely criticised launch - and as the legendary 4X series celebrates its 35th anniversary - Firaxis unveiled a host of latest updates coming to the game as it continued to improve it. These included an atomic age upgrade, dragging Civ 7 into the present and beyond, as well as its first paid expansion, Earthrise, both arriving next year.

Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick admitted earlier this year that the studio "got it wrong with Civ 7".

Industry observers note that "The game is a really good game. And it's certainly a profitable enterprise for us. But this is one where I think what we tried to do was a bridge too far, from the consumer's perspective," he told Game File in May.

It’s not the first round of cuts at the studio - 2K confirmed an unspecified number of layoffs at Firaxis in September 2025, and around 30 jobs went in 2023.

Here is an overview of the game, via Giant Light Studios:.

Industry observers note that blending Minesweeper-inspired deduction, push-your-luck mechanics, and roguelike deckbuilding, Mr. Magpie’s Harmless Card Game traps players in a twisted corporate office, where they are forced to play by a smiling puppet host who insists everything is under control.

In a recent development, with Behaviour Interactive, the studio behind globally recognized horror experiences such as Dead by Daylight and 7 Days to Die, joining as publisher, Mr. Magpie’s Harmless Card Game strengthens its connection to a large and dedicated horror audience.

Together with Gambit Digital, the team is preparing to bring the game to players with expanded visibility and support throughout development and into launch.

Each run revolves around flipping cards to generate money and multipliers while using hints to deduce the location of dangerous JERRY cards. Push your luck too far, and the run collapses.

Stack the deck in your favor, exploit strange synergies, and make your quota before closing time… or else.

Runs are short, decisions are risky, and every card flip is a calculated gamble as players climb the corporate ladder. The further they progress, the stranger the office becomes.

Between runs, players can explore the workplace, uncover fragments of the company’s disturbing history, and slowly understand why Mr. Magpie seems so invested in the outcome.

In short, yes. Though they aren't quite as impactful as they once were, Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales offer discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. Whether it's a major purchase you've been saving up for or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts, especially on items like appliances and electronics. Industry observers note that is there something going on today? A lot of talk about committing crimes and the like, I just can't quite put my finger on why… Ah well, couldn't be crucial or interesting. What is interesting, however, is Keepsake County, a "midwestern stealth game" that has launched on this inauspicious day about stealing stuff from "hideous farmhouses in the middle of nowhere.".

With the sarcastic intro out the way, I will address the elephant in the room: Vovly's Adventure: Reslimed is out today too. Fine, fine, yes I know GTA 6 is the game everyone's talking about, but Forward Instinct, the devs behind Keepsake County, seem well aware of that in their launch day post for the game: "Folks, thanks for your incredible patience. Keepsake County is finally OUT! And yes, it is deeply ironic that it wound up being today, of all days, that we got the green light to finally release, but here we are.".

It has been revealed that keepsake Country was supposed to release earlier this month, but seemingly got caught up in the backlog Valve are faced with that's undoubtedly been caused by genAI games. In any case, the burgle-em-up does look quite delightful. I'm not sure if I can quite put my finger on exactly why I get this feeling, but it calls to mind a more complex version of the kind of game you'd find on Cartoon Network's website back in the day (which is a high point of praise, I'd like to be clear).

Each house in Keepsake Country is procedurally generated, meaning you never quite know what to expect when you enter. There's lockpicking, resident tie upping, and of course stealing to be done, but it doesn't just stop at the house. Parking your car, for instance, is an important thing to consider; do you want it hidden so you're less likely to be discovered, or right at the front door so you can make a speedy escape? Not to mention you have to deal with the fuzz showing up at some point if you aren't quick enough!

Industry observers note that gear and the like can be improved between runs, meaning you can lockpick faster or delay the cops, it all seems quite systemically thoughtful. Very much some immersive sim vibes from this one, just on a much smaller scale. And most certainly worth considering picking up on a release day like today! Industry observers note that A upcoming Fallout game is indeed on the way, but it's not what you're expecting. Bethesda's next post-apocalyptic project is in fact a cat-themed hidden object game.

Earlier this week, a listing from the Australian Classifications Board accidentally spilled information about a game called A Wasteland Full of Cats. The now-deleted description let slip that it's a hidden object game - think Where's Wally/Waldo - where you need to find cats in some of the series' underground Vaults and the dangerous radioactive lands outside.

Recent findings suggest that "You play as one of the cats in the Vault. One day there is an accident in the Vault and all of the cats who live there escape out into the Wasteland. It is up to you with the help of some NPCs you meet along the way to find them and return them to the Vault," according to the listing.

It has been revealed that "This game has 14 locations, 33 rooms + a vault of recognizable levels from the Fallout franchise with light puzzle mechanics that uncover some hidden levels that aren't required to finish the game. There is a final boss fight where the player has to shoot some Rad roaches in order to save the last remaining cats and humans. This game will be part of Devcats 'Full of Cats' series of cats and plays like the other games in the series. This game is in partnership with Bethesda and the Fallout franchise.".

It didn't take long for series owner Bethesda to confirm the leak, either. "Cat's out of the bag," the studio writes on social media, explaining that it's partnered with non-profit animal charity Dallas Pets Alive and developer Devcat Games on the "Fallout-inspired adventure.".

There's no trailer or release date yet, but Bethesda claims it'll "have more to share soon.".

If finding hard-to-spot felines sounds like your vibe, Devcat Games has a ton of other games in the Full of Cats series, whether you're into exploring castles or flats or outer space.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

A Wasteland Full of Cats might not be the Fallout game fans were expecting after the company formally announced remasters for Fallout 3 and Fallout: Latest Vegas, alongside a new game from Obsidian Entertainment, but it sounds like a cute stop over along the way. Fallout 5 is also in early pre-production.

Fallout 5 being set outside the US "could be amazing," former Bethesda lead notes, even if Todd Howard has previously suggested it's not happening.

Featuring a crunchy PSX-inspired aesthetic and tense isometric to first-person perspective switching gameplay, echograph delivers a stylish and highly-atmospheric take on a beloved genre.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • "When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'.

"When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business. "People didn't think it looked good. Then Pixar launched Toy Story. They created a movie that not only was awesome, but used computer-generated animation and chose a subject matter that made the most of it, and did an amazing job with it.".

Feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games. Feder added, "My own view is that we are one Toy Story moment away from consumer acceptance of AI in video games in the West. In the East, they've already accepted it.".

Feder, who presently heads up venture capital fund Tirta Ventures, is investing in AI-first games. He, however, doesn't necessarily believe AI will reduce development costs, but that it also offers other advantages that could help game makers keep up with shifting consumer tastes.

"A lot of incumbents think about AI as a way of reducing costs, which it is," Feder noted. "I query whether it will actually reduce costs, or will it just make games bigger for the same cost? But we're more interested in what AI can do to radically change gameplay.".

According to recent reports, feder views gen-AI simply as new technology that allows developers to do things they couldn't before. He likened it to Unreal Engine's instancing technology, which allowed Fortnite and other battle royale games to support 100+ players in a single server.

In a recent development, "That's question number one as we think about what we invest in: Was this possible before AI?" Feder remarked of his VC firm's strategy. "And when AI gets better, does the game get better? That's harder for an incumbent to focus on, because they deploy a lot of capital, have enormous advantages in terms of distribution, capital, and IP, and all of that needs to be protected.".

There's been enormous pushback from players, developers and pundits against the use of gen-AI in games. Even so, more and more studios have revealed using some gen-AI during development, such as to assist with coding. More broadly, gen-AI adoption is on the rise across the industry, with a recent report estimating 40 percent of developers are using it.

Sources indicate that some development studios, such as Fortnite maker Epic Games, have doubled down on the use of gen-AI in game development. Epic is even more bullish on gen-AI in its Unreal Engine, which the firm is at the moment transforming into an engine that's almost entirely driven by gen-AI and LLMs. Consumer sentiment remains sour, however, and the perception of the tool is not helped by the number of 'AI slop' games taking over Steam's storefront, the 'enshittification' of fan wikis, or the link AI seems to have to the unprecedented wave of layoffs that has shaken the industry over the past two years.

Space station horror-FPS Derelikt is a lively retro throwback to Alien: Resurrection, though it's better at shooting than scaring

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (699 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery.
  • In a recent development, still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well.
  • It turns out Derelikt's derelict dwellers are both perfectly susceptible to mundane lead, and sparing users of ambush tactics at most; several even stand around with their backs turned, as if waiting for you to surprise them with a lethal pipe swing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I'm a reasonable man. I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery. Some of the lighter moments in Derelikt, which released last week, even land: I was grinning my cheeks off as I gorged on the Eldtrich knowledge sealed within an alien obelisk, while repeatedly hanging up on the aghast scientist who kept videocalling me to stop.

In a recent development, still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well. It certainly threatens the spooks, trapping you in an oppressively dingy asteroid rig in the orbit of Saturn - the scariest of the ringed gas giants! - and warping most of the other staff into vaguely echinodemic monsterpeople. Also, opening the inventory reveals it to be made of rectangles, a classic symptom of a video game character about to get mangled in the nerves and face.

But nah, shotgun go boom boom. It turns out Derelikt's derelict dwellers are both perfectly susceptible to mundane lead, and sparing users of ambush tactics at most; several even stand around with their backs turned, as if waiting for you to surprise them with a lethal pipe swing. And, even on Medium difficulty, the opening spell of fight-or-run scarcity rapidly gives way to an abundance of ammo and health pickups that can easily fill the pocket grid to bursting. I don't claim to have been playing perfectly, but I'm about halfway through and the only way I see myself running low on bullets is if I start using them to punch the complete works of Thomas Campion into a wall.

It's indecisive tonally, as well. The dialogue, and there are a fair few survivors to chat with, seems interested in emulating the gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style of Latest Millennium action game scripts. Which I can sort of see the logic behind, given the visuals and sound design also, and arguably much more painstakingly, mimic that era. But the downside remains that it ends up with a gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style, just with an extra dash of sideways-winking awareness. Again, it only sometimes works, and it's never scary or eerie. But then there are also more earnest attempts to spin uneasiness, with pages of deranged scribbles left behind by the dwindling crew, and at least a couple of genre-classic wall daubings, which tend to leave me wishing developers Visuwyg had just picked a lane.

Again, though, underneath all the smartarsing is a quality little shooter. The retro presentation does little to soften the heavy, industrial kick of its gunfire, and although many of the meatier freaks are more absorbent than they look, their pained thrashing really helps sell the impact of every individual shot. I also don't really mind the lack of Dead Spacey surprise attacks, as the station's narrow confines tend to force you into tenser, close-range encounters in an organic way anyhow.

More impressive still is how Derelikt manages to fabricate a cold, apprehensive atmosphere befitting its fallen space base, in direct defiance of its own quasi-comedic script. This is mainly thanks to the clanging, low-lit station itself, which teases you with just enough flashes of comfort – a stretch of marble floor here, a messy rec room there – to make your quick return to its steel guts feel all the more unpleasant. Some credit must also go to the puzzling, the cardkey hunts and code searches of which initially had me fearful of the more obstinate, opaque, classic horror style preferred by fellow backwards-looker Silver Pines. Instead, it's more like a compacted Deus Ex, hinting at the need to peek at people's computers and scour the environments for the needed codes. Which makes for generally smoother progress, yes, but also gets you more involved and present inside Derelikt's infested walls.

Industry observers note that midway-through impressions, then: it's a little silly, and perhaps a little confused, but Derelikt finds its focus whenever something needs making dead. I shall continue blasting xenos and burning my eyes out with magic rocks until – no, madam, please hold – further notice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto 6 is already enormously successful, having enjoyed "the biggest entertainment launch in history". But the current games industry is such that some Rockstar developers are still concerned about being laid off in the wake of its release. Writing for the Guardian prior to GTA 6's launch, Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte explained that although there is "no indication that layoffs are coming" it nonetheless "says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off.".

Recent findings suggest that it might sound odd for the developers of such a hugely successful game to be worried about losing their jobs, but layoffs don't just occur when games or companies struggle commercially. A common cause of layoffs in the games industry is companies trying to reduce overheads after a game has released, as the studio switches from full production to post-release support for their current game and planning for the next one.

Recent findings suggest that it's partly why the industry seems to be in a constant, rolling state of layoffs, even when games appear to sell well. This matter was recently addressed by Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. Svedberg-Yen, who left Sandfall Interactive in July, claimed that the problem is exacerbated by an imbalance in who benefits financially when a game like Grand Theft Auto 6 launches.

Sources indicate that "99 Metacritic score. Multiple award nominations before it even released. Massive sales and player engagement. Incredible amounts of tangible and intangible value creation. Yet the team is worried about layoffs," Svedberg-Yen wrote in an Instagram post. "So, who receives the lion's share of the profits from their labor? Not the vast majority of the creative team.".

Svedberg-Yen pointed out that this is "one of the issues that happens when the people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value," adding that "In finance, we call that value extraction.".

Svedberg-Yen also commented on the Rockstar team's ongoing efforts to unionise, with the team in the process of voting on whether or not it wants a union. If successful, the Rockstar Game Workers Union would become the biggest in the UK's gaming sector.

It has been revealed that "I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing," Svedberg-Yen wrote. "Layoffs during lulls in development cycles would work a lot better if teams were properly paid for the value they create, not just one-time, but throughout the life of the thing they created.".

Most recently, Firaxis, owned by GTA 6 publisher Take Two Interactive, reportedly laid off a third of its staff earlier this week as it works on a upcoming XCOM.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability update. The dinky SteamOS PC continues to have a terrible time with AI industry-inflicted hardware parts shortages, which at least for its flagship 2TB model, have become such a problem that Valve are suspending new orders until further notice. While Valve's post says that they "have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders" – meaning if you'd previously reserved one, you'll still get your chance to buy – "supply restraints" have put the kibosh on any new orders for now.

Industry observers note that it's not all bad news, though. The cheaper 512GB Steam Machine has achieved "add-to-cart status", which is Valve's slightly odd way of saying you can snap one up without having to join a reservation waitlist. Just like in the Before Times! The post does add that 512GB stock is still limited, so that might sell out too if they can't source enough parts to build latest ones, though this is still the first time that the refreshed Steam Machine has been waitlist-free since launching in June.

It has been revealed that one could, with the aid of a Torx screwdriver and a conveniently illustrated guide, work around the 2TB model's lack of existence by nabbing a readily available 512GB Machine and replacing its stock SSD with a chunkier aftermarket drive. A not-terrible, budget two-gigster can be had from £240, which when added to the 512GB Machine's £879 outlay, actually works out a little less than buying a 2TB Machine as is. SteamOS is free to download and install, and swapping out the Steam Machine's SSD is considerably easier than the plasticky brain surgery of Steam Deck drive replacement.

Industry observers note that of course, ideally none of that would be necessary, and we could all fill our living rooms with sub-£700 Steam Machines that had never been choked by the greedy hands of industrial-scale RAM hoarders. But that's not the world we live in. Indeed, Valve end the post by rather chillingly suggesting that their hardware prices may rise yet again.

It has been revealed that "We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units," they say, "but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained.".

"We anticipate having more information to share come January.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard.
  • Industry observers note that for those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the new late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard. Suspensions have been issued, trade locks have been put on accounts, and ill-gotten gold is being seized.

Industry observers note that for those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the new late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold. By quickly clearing select mobs with area-of-effect damage, players would loot upwards of 100 raw gold an hour. This exploit, clearly not intentional, was nonetheless farmed until Blizzard hotfixed it earlier in the week.

In a recent development, there was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit. That speculation would come to an end late last night with an official statement from the World of Warcraft: Forever development team.

"As players continue their journey into WoW Forever’s higher-level content, we are closely monitoring the game economy to ensure that gold sources and costs are well balanced," the statement reads. "Finding efficient farming spots has always been part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest.".

It goes on to explain the nature of the bug that made this gold farm possible, before reassuring those who may have accidentally benefited from some extra cash from their regular runs of Blackmaw Hold they have nothing to worry about. The same cannot be stated for those who took advantage of the situation.

"Players who simply ran Blackmaw Hold a few times and benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong, and no one should worry that they’re putting their account at risk if they accidentally benefit from a bug," it continues. "But there were a couple hundred players worldwide who recognized that this was unintended and spent significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies.

"Yesterday, we put an economy lock on their accounts to prevent broader impact to the game economy while we investigated the extent of the exploitative gains, including gold earned by vendoring bugged drops. Today, we are in the process of removing all such gold earned, as well as applying account suspensions to significant abusers.".

The post concludes by thanking players for their feedback on the matter, and a final warning: "As always, we advise all players to refrain from abusing game mechanics that are clearly unintended. We will continue to take action against intentional abuse.".

This decision certainly sets the precedent moving forward with World of Warcraft: Forever that such exploits won't be tolerated, and rolling back the wealth of those who made out of Blackmaw Hold like bandits is a good measure that should prevent continuous damage.

It has been revealed that inevitably the exploit would have had some impact, specifically in those days prior to trading blocks being put in place. While the gold on the exploiter's accounts may be removed, any purchases they made on the in-game auction house will have affected others through buying and selling goods with ample funds.

In a recent development, those who were suspended temporarily will be able to regain access to the game by the time the first wave of raids come out in December, so it very much feels like a firm slap on the wrist in that regard. Even so, given the establishment of punishments for such behavior, one can only wonder if future events will come with harsher penalties.

It has been revealed that world of Warcraft: Forever, despite this small economic roadbump, is proving exceptionally popular for Blizzard. It's already broken records for the series, and has impressed players so far with its revamping of the classic MMO.

There are two methods of getting GTA 6 safe codes:.

These are the set GTA 6 safe codes that are the same for every player:.

Sources indicate that motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the firm trumpeted that their "newly introduced operating model" is "now fully in place".
