#85995. 10 Privacy Hacks Every Mac User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1051 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

10 Privacy Hacks Every Mac User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1051 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple has a pretty good track record on privacy.
  • Enabling the macOS Firewall (which is off by default) adds a layer of protection against external devices on your wifi network, as well as unauthorized apps from initiating a connection to your device.
  • According to recent reports, another hack for maintaining privacy on public networks is to enable rotating MAC addresses, which randomizes the identifier your device broadcasts when scanning for and connecting to wifi.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has a pretty good track record on privacy. The company bakes a number of protections into its OSes to keep your data from being shared or stolen. That mentioned, you can make your Apple devices even more secure. There are plenty of opt-in settings that make it even harder for anyone to snoop on your device and activity. These are the best privacy hacks for your Mac.

Enabling the macOS Firewall (which is off by default) adds a layer of protection against external devices on your wifi network, as well as unauthorized apps from initiating a connection to your device. Turning on Stealth Mode prevents your Mac from even responding to these requests, essentially making it invisible to anything that's scanning a network you're connected to. This makes it more difficult for hackers and malware to know your device exists, much less attack it. This can interfere with certain essential activity when you're on your home network, but it's a valuable security setting when on public wifi. You can leave Firewall on all the time and enable Stealth Mode only as needed. Go to Settings > Network > Firewall, flip the toggle, then hit Options to manage Stealth Mode.

According to recent reports, another hack for maintaining privacy on public networks is to enable rotating MAC addresses, which randomizes the identifier your device broadcasts when scanning for and connecting to wifi. If you use either your real MAC address or a fixed one (random but unchanging), it's easier to track your activity on that network, including when you arrive, how long you stay, and when you leave. Rotating addresses are best for public, shared networks you temporarily connect to, and don't require a login via a captive portal (like hotel wifi). You can turn this on for specific networks via Settings > Wi-Fi > [Network Name] > Details and change Private Wi-Fi address to Rotating.

Images and screenshots contain metadata, such as timestamps, device and hardware details, and, in the case of photos, physical location. Much of this information is stripped automatically when you share files to social media or via encrypted messaging apps, but if you're sending them via text or email, posting to forums, or sharing over AirDrop, metadata remains intact. You can easily remove metadata from your images right on your desktop. Select the file and hit control + click to bring up an options menu, then go to Quick Actions > Convert Image. Uncheck the box next to Preserve Metadata, then hit Convert. (This is also useful for quickly converting HEIC to JPEG without opening a separate app.).

Industry observers note that apple collects information about your device for diagnostic purposes or to improve apps and services, some of which is shared with third-party app developers. This may include crash and usage data as well as recordings and transcripts of Siri interactions and iCloud analytics. You can disable sharing for some or all of these categories under Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.

According to recent reports, you may be surprised by the number of apps and system services that use your device's location in the background. You should definitely disable location services for third-party apps that don't require location to function. You can find these toggles under Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services. You can also turn off location permissions for some Apple apps and services if you're not using them on your device, like Weather and Maps. Finally, tap System Services and disable location for any non-essential features—at the very least, disable "Mac Analytics" and "Significant Locations & routes" (which lets your Mac and other iCloud devices learn locations and routes you use often).

Third-party apps on your Mac that need access to your device's camera and microphone have to request permission, and it's easy to grant this in the moment and then forget that you've allowed it. You should regularly audit which apps have these permissions and revoke access from those that don't need them on a day-to-day basis. Disabling them forces the app to ask again. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone or Camera to see the allowed apps and flip the toggle to disable permissions.

Another permission type you may have granted without much thought is local network access. This allows third-party apps to discover and communicate with other devices—printers, smart speakers, and IoT devices—on your home wifi. While this may be useful for services like Spotify that cast to connected hardware, other utilities, media apps, and games probably don't need to be mapping your network in the background. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network to audit permissions and disable those that aren't needed.

Sources indicate that another important permission to check concerns third-party apps that have access to your Mac's full disk, which includes data from Mail, Messages, Safari, Home, Time Machine, and admin settings. If an app only works with files you explicitly open and save, it doesn't need full disk access. Legitimate use cases may include antivirus and malware scanners, productivity tools, or backup utilities that you trust. You can also audit which apps have access to specific files and folders. This is under Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access or Files & Folders.

Industry observers note that if you're using iCloud to store photos, files, and device backups, your data is encrypted on Apple's servers and in transit. Apple still holds the decryption key, which is useful if you somehow get locked out of your account and need help recovering it, but for sensitive data—including device backups—end-to-end encryption is the most secure way to ensure no one but you can gain access. Advanced Data Protection is an opt-in setting for iCloud that encrypts your information end to end. You'll need to set up an alternative recovery method, such as your device passcode with two-factor authentication, a recovery contact, or a recovery key. Be careful, though: If you lose access to this recovery method, you will lose your data. You can enable Advanced Data Protection on your Mac under System Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > Advanced Data Protection > Turn On. Note that some iCloud data, including passwords and payment methods, are already end-to-end encrypted by default.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The chance to shake Mattia's hand in GTA 6 comes up right at the start of the mission Day Release, seemingly like a key decision that might affect the tone of the rest of the mission and future job prospects. Multiple GamesRadar+ writers have gone through both options, and it's a lot less crucial of a decision in GTA 6 than you think, so here's what we know about the significance of shaking Mattia's hand.

Be aware of some very mild spoilers for later missions in Chapter 1 below.

Shaking Mattia's hand in GTA 6 makes no difference to any events in the Day Release mission. If you shake his hand, you shake his hand, and if you don't, you don't. Mattia doesn't even acknowledge that you left him hanging.

According to recent reports, later in the mission, Mattia offers Jason and Lucia some drugs in a nightclub and, again, accepting or refusing has no clear repercussions. Comparing videos of the choices side-by-side, there were no obvious differences between either outcome as the same thing happens regardless - Mattia either takes the drugs back or hands them over, stands up and leaves, then Jason and Lucia take to the dancefloor. The rest of the mission then plays out as normal.

As far as I can tell, turning Mattia down in either of these situations in Day Release has no long-term impact either as the "job" that he mentions at the end of the mission is critical to the story and can't be avoided. Just make sure you've done everything before the GTA 6 Tourist Trap mission as it's an key one – and if you get stuck, my GTA 6 Tourist Trap walkthrough can help.

We've also got loads of other GTA 6 guides for you to read if you're ever stuck.

How To Solve All Main Puzzles In GTA 6′s Tenebrae Lux

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1593 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Kotaku

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you decide you’d rather sit at home all day and play a pretentious, cerebral puzzle game instead of go on heists, Tenebrae Lux is waiting for Jason and Lucia on their JoyStation in GTA VI.
  • But I’m assuming you’re here because you either want to beat it rapidly, or you’ve gotten so stuck (as I did) on a few of the puzzles that you’re desperate for help.
  • Industry observers note that you’ll start out on the shoreline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6Grand Theft Auto VI.

If you decide you’d rather sit at home all day and play a pretentious, cerebral puzzle game instead of go on heists, Tenebrae Lux is waiting for Jason and Lucia on their JoyStation in GTA VI. While on the surface it looks like just a funny gag poking at auteur culture (and one developer in particular), Tenebrae Lux is a surprisingly solid, short puzzle game that (if you’re not using this guide) may take you a few hours to get through.

But I’m assuming you’re here because you either want to beat it rapidly, or you’ve gotten so stuck (as I did) on a few of the puzzles that you’re desperate for help. I get you. Here’s as simple a walkthrough as I could manage for Tenebrae Lux:.

Industry observers note that you’ll start out on the shoreline. You can’t do much: just walk around and examine objects. To start with, you’re going to want to head to the left side of the shore (assuming you’re facing the shore from the beach you start on) where there are multiple run-down shacks lit by substantial bright lights.

Inside these shacks are three puzzles on gridded boards. On those grids, multiple pieces are placed with different 3D shapes atop: three-tiered tall ones, middling spiky ones, and flat ones with a tiny dot in the middle. The flat ones don’t move at all, the middle-sized spiky ones can slide across the board and clear the flat ones if they land next to them, and the three-tiered tall ones and middle-sized ones clear one another in the same fashion. Your goal is to clear all the pieces off the board.

You can do these puzzles in any order. One of them is easy and straightforward, but the other two require a little bit more thinking. You’ll have to use the fact that the flat pieces don’t move and cannot be cleared by the three-tiered pieces to set up the three-tiers so they and the mountain pieces can clear one another once all the flat ones are off the board.

It has been revealed that the three main puzzles in this area should be fairly simple to do, though there are a couple of hidden ones you can optionally do that are more difficult. On at least one, you might need to set up your board so you have two three-tier pieces set up with a gap between them that a middle-sized piece can easily get into after clearing a flat one. See below:.

When I move that mountain-shaped piece to the left, it will take out itself and all three of those other tiles with it.

This puzzle will easily make you feel like you’re losing your mind, but I highly recommend trying to work it out for yourself first, if you can.

Sources indicate that when you enter the room upstairs in the bunker, you enter a loop that will keep perpetuating each time you go through the door and up the stairs. The room will be almost identical each time you enter it, but for two things. The first will be the calendar, which will show the date as being one of six different dates, and the second will be one of the other objects in the room.

Your goal is to find a six-digit code and enter it into the phone, followed by the # sign, to proceed.

In order to get the code, you need to pay attention to what day it is, and what is different in the room on that date. If you keep going up the stairs over and over, the dates will eventually cycle back through, so if you miss one don’t worry, you can keep going to see it again. The dates are as follows: October 11, 14, 20, 23, 27, and 30. You won’t see the dates in any particular order, but you’ll need to put them in that order when you input the numbers for each date into the phone.

Sources indicate that the numbers themselves, you get from finding what’s “different” in the room on a given date, and working out what number the difference corresponds to. There are ten possible differences, and your playthrough won’t have all these objects in the roomâit’s random each time, though consistent within a single playthrough of the puzzle. Here are the ten possible differences:.

Once you get the code right, exit upwards one last time and on you go.

This one was waaaaay more confusing to me than it needed to be. The goal is to cross the bridge off to the left of the ruins. The bridge has multiple rows of weird symbols on it. You have to walk over the correct symbol in order to proceed. If you walk over the wrong one, a lamp will go out. If you do it wrong three times, you fail and the puzzle resets.

The trick to figuring out the correct symbols is in the ruins and the poem on the plaque just outside.

The ruins will contain the following items, which correspond to the following descriptors in each of the seven lines of the poem:.

In a recent development, the items will be scattered across the ruins. Also in the ruins you will find a bunch of weird, esoteric symbols glowing on the ruined archways above. These symbols correspond to the symbols on the bridge.

To solve this, you need to visit each of the items in the order they appear in the poem, and match the item with the symbol on the ruins that corresponds to it, then follow the symbols across the bridge in order (the direction they’re facing doesn’t matter). It can be a bit tricky to figure out which symbol goes with which item. The best way I can describe it is the symbol for each item is the one that’s over the doorway “entrance” to each item, so the one you have to pass under to reach it.

Here’s a map to show you what I mean. Orange circles are places where the objects can appear, and green triangles are where symbols are. I’ve numbered them, but please don’t mistake the numbers for the correctÂ order of the objects: that’s going to be determined by the poem, and the poem’s order is random.

Also note that #1 below is on the ground, because the arch has collapsed.

According to recent reports, this can still be confusing, so let me walk you through what I got as an example. Here’s my poem:.

First up is moon, which for me was straight ahead through the first door.

Two days of rest says nothing, so we move to the third line, which mentions forests. Here’s the tree:.

Recent findings suggest that third verse mentions gold, then earth, in order. My trophy was past the mark that had crumbled to the ground, and my earth was at the very start of the puzzle:.

Industry observers note that this next line is a bit tricky, as it mentions both sun and moon. But there are only seven lines on the bridge, and the items are only used one time each. So we just focus on sun here. I didn’t get a good picture of my sundial, sorry!

The last two lines in order mentions fire first, then drinking, which is water. Here’s fire:.

In a recent development, so I’d follow those symbols in order across the bridge. It may help to draw a map on a piece of scrap paper or in a notebook for this one so you don’t have to slowly walk back and forth over and over.

If you fail, the puzzle will fully reset itself, and you’ll have to look at a newly introduced version of the poem and ruins and try again.

This bit is a little creepy and again confusing at first, but quite easy once you work it out. All you have to do is walk in the door that’s the furthest away from any of the figures walking through the doors.

In the photo above, the man is walking toward the third door from the right, so I want to go to the farthest door on the left.

In a recent development, as you go, more figures will start to appear. When there are multiple, you want to try and split the distance as best as possible. You also have to avoid any doors that say they’re out of order, so if they have a sign on them, go to the next one furthest away from the man. On the last set of doors, there was no way to get away from the men, so I just walked directly between two of them.

Once you pass through the last door, you’ve officially beaten Tenebrae Lux!

If you were curious how accurate the utility towers in Grand Theft Auto 6 the answer appears to be: Very.

The best way to play is just to experience the game, even if most of us are too internet-pilled to do that.

People don't like having to scroll a big number back and forth to deposit a specific amount.

It's a funny ad poking fun at another massive franchise, but is a bit awkward as Rockstar deals with its own employees trying to form a union.

I could see an HBO TV adaptation of Red Dead Redemption making sense.

Tech Report: If Your Google Pixel's Camera Is Suddenly Broken, Here's the Fix

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updates are generally good for your devices.
  • Recent findings suggest that sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel users are discovering this week.
  • Here's the situation: Following the November update, some owners are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updates are generally good for your devices. The latest Chrome update, for example, patches an actively exploited security vulnerability, while Apple's latest updates stop people from seeing iMessages they shouldn't have access to. In most cases, it's beneficial to update your tech to the latest software version whenever possible.

Recent findings suggest that sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel users are discovering this week. As reported by Android Authority, Google's November update apparently shipped with a bug that breaks some Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 cameras. Seeing as Pixels are rather famous for their shooters, this is a decidedly unfortunate glitch.

Here's the situation: Following the November update, some owners are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong. Close and open the Camera app again," with a "Learn More" link to, well, learn more. Others aren't receiving the error, but are instead running into a blank Camera viewfinder, as if the lens is totally covered. What's more, some users are reportedly saying that the issue is present on third-party camera apps, not just the Pixel Camera app. That would imply this is an issue with the camera system-wide, not just the Pixel Camera app itself.

Sources indicate that to be clear, it doesn't seem like this is a universal issue. It's not like all Pixel consumers are now running with broken cameras. But based on the forum complaints Android Authority discovered, it seems reasonable to assume that this glitch isn't limited to just a handful of unlucky Pixel owners.

Luckily, there is an apparent workaround here, though it's not totally obvious. Some people are having no luck restarting their Pixels, while others report that a factory reset wasn't enough to restore camera functionality.

According to recent reports, what does appear to work, however, is shutting your Pixel down and waiting five minutes or so. It's not clear why, but giving your Pixel a chance to "breathe" seems to shake the glitch and bring back your camera. As Android Authority reports, that fix comes from "Diamond and Gold product experts" on Google's Support forum.

If your Pixel's camera is giving you grief following the November update, this workaround is definitely worth a try—especially since more drastic measures don't actually seem to do anything. As the issue does seem to be rather widespread, I wouldn't be surprised to see Google issue a patch in the coming days. But until then, turning your phone off for five minutes may be a decent compromise.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is hitting a significant milestone this year and will be turning the substantial 100.
  • Sources indicate that the beloved hippo became a global sensation following her premature birth in January 2017, and after receiving round-the-clock care, she began to thrive.
  • Sources indicate that in addition to the balloon possibly representing Fiona, it also has a long, legendary history.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is hitting a significant milestone this year and will be turning the substantial 100. To celebrate, they are pulling out all the stops, including adding favorites, both fresh and old. One returning balloon has fans emotional as the announcement comes after the tragic death of Fiona the Hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden. Now that Macy’s has brought back its blue hippo for the 100th parade, Fiona fans have a request.

Sources indicate that the beloved hippo became a global sensation following her premature birth in January 2017, and after receiving round-the-clock care, she began to thrive. She was also the first Nile hippo to be imaged prenatally via ultrasound at the zoo and the first born there in 75 years. However, on November 19, she swallowed a knit hat that was accidentally tossed into her enclosure, and it tragically led to her premature death. The loss hit hard for a lot of fans. One Reddit thread suggests that Macy’s blue hippopotamus “should totally dedicate it to Fiona,” and it has fans responding with comments like:.

Sources indicate that in addition to the balloon possibly representing Fiona, it also has a long, legendary history. It was first unveiled in 1931, and during that parade, they decided it was a good idea to release giant balloons into New York City. You may be asking yourself, why? I’ll tell you. Each balloon had a price tag, and whoever found a balloon and returned it to the department store would receive that amount as a prize. The blue hippo balloon was never returned, and even after an offer of $100, nobody came forward, leaving the balloon lost to history.

To ring in the parade’s substantial birthday, they’ve decided to bring back the blue hippo, but this time, it’ll keep its feet tethered to the ground. It will be joining an assortment of fresh additions, including everything from KPop Demon Hunters to Bluey. There’s something for everyone in the family to enjoy, and if you weren’t already, this year’s celebration could make you become a parade person.

The new balloon is reportedly going to look like a more modern version of the 1931 balloon seen below:.

Sources indicate that if the blue hippo isn’t enough to sell you on the parade, then maybe some upcoming floats might. We’ll be seeing a variety of newcomers, including "Hogwarts Holiday," which features a Harry Potter-themed float that will celebrate (and promote) the newly rebooted series on HBO kicking off in December. The cool floats and balloons are an opportunity for brands (like Starbucks) to promote themselves with whimsical, colorful, and unique floats or balloons.

Additionally, it will include Tom Jr., which is a fresh turkey addition to the parade, and Tony Sarg’s Amazing Marionettes, which pays tribute to the original parade puppeteer. There is also a mix of performers to look forward to, including The Voice’s new favorite coach, Queen Latifah.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

However, a lot of Fiona fans will be watching to catch sight of the blue hippo and are hopeful it will do her justice with a sweet tribute or at least a special place in the parade.

Sources indicate that the big event will hit the 2026 TV schedule on Thanksgiving Day, November 26, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. across time zones. This can be viewed on NBC, Telemundo, or with a Peacock subscription.

So Is The $100 GTA 6 Ultimate Edition Actually Worth It?

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (995 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Kotaku

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that before Grand Theft Auto 6 even launched, there was some controversy online over the announcement of a $100 “Ultimate Edition” version of the game that would include access to a few exclusive shops and in-game cosmetics.
  • Recent findings suggest that in GTA 6, there are five stores that are locked behind the Ultimate Edition paywall.
  • First up, there’s 305, a clothing store specializing in urban, skater-inspired clothing and gear.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that before Grand Theft Auto 6 even launched, there was some controversy online over the announcement of a $100 “Ultimate Edition” version of the game that would include access to a few exclusive shops and in-game cosmetics. So, now that GTA 6 is here and I’ve spent over 150 hours with it, I can share what’s in the Ultimate Edition, how you access this stuff, and if it’s worth upgrading from the standard $80 version of GTA 6. The short version is…eh, probably not.

Recent findings suggest that in GTA 6, there are five stores that are locked behind the Ultimate Edition paywall. These stores include an exclusive tattoo parlor, street clothing shop, and hair salon. Now, at first, I thought it was pretty shitty of Rockstar to hide stores behind a paywall. And to be clear, it still does suck that a few shops are only accessible if you pay $20 more. But after playing GTA 6, I discovered that the world is filled with over 600 stores. There are already so many clothing, car, hair, make-up, and nail options in the base game. So the Ultimate Edition’s extra few stores don’t feel that necessary. And after actually visiting these shops and seeing what they have to offer, I don’t think people are missing out on that much.

First up, there’s 305, a clothing store specializing in urban, skater-inspired clothing and gear. There’s some alright stuff in here, including some nice-looking jeans for Jason and a cool graphic shirt or two. And a really wild fuzzy hat for Lucia. But the options in here aren’t something you need to have. You can create plenty of great and cool outfits without stopping by this Ultimate Editionâonly retailer.

Sources indicate that next up is the tattoo shop Electric Fang. Of all the Ultimate Edition stores, this is the coolest one to enter. And I do think some of Electric Fang’s tat designs are solid. But again, there are so many other options in the game for ink that I’m not sure these are very necessary or worth the $20 upgrade.

It has been revealed that sara’s Unisex Salon might be the best of the bunch as it offers some stylish hairdos for both Jason and Lucia. But on top of that, it offers some really nice makeup options for Lucia and cool nail art, too. I ended up using some of these options during my time as Lucia because I liked them so much. Still, again, there are so many other good options for haircuts and nail art already in GTA 6 that I’m not sure you need to spend $20 more on this version.

There are also two exclusive car mod garages in GTA 6‘s Ultimate Edition. One of them, Rideout Customs, offers some really gaudy and exotic paint and accessories options. If you wanted a neon-pink car with stripes painted to look like cheetah print, well, this is the place for you.

It has been revealed that the other mod shop, One-Eyed Willie’s, is more useful. It offers up some really nice off-road options. There aren’t nearly as many off-road modding options in GTA 6 as there are for street cars, so losing out on access to this in the base game is a shame. I also love that One-Eyed Willie’s offers up a random paint job for every car in the game, including non-off-road vehicles, that you can only see once it’s applied. I brought my Banshee into the shop, and it received this pretty pink design that I loved.

The Ultimate Edition also includes some unique free clothing items based on characters from an in-universe cartoon you can watch. These clothes are fine. I guess if you like the show a lot, they might be fun to wear. But…eh.

Beyond the stores and cosmetics, there are some exclusive vehicles you get access to in the Ultimate Edition, but some of these are only available during chapter one for story reasons. The only thing from the Ultimate Edition I used regularly and still use often when I play is the Vapid off-road truck. It’s fast as heck, a great option for driving on the dirt, and can be upgraded into a beast that can hold a lot of stolen loot. There’s also a classic car scavenger hunt side mission hidden behind the paywall, but after 150 hours I’ve barely interacted with that thing.

In a recent development, answering the big question of “Is the Ultimate Edition worth it?” is tricky, because it depends entirely on what you value and your taste for fashion and cosmetics. I’ve provided some samples of what’s on offer and how it fits into the larger GTA 6 world.

My opinion is that if you can afford the extra $20, a few bits of the Ultimate Edition are nice and worth the upgrade. But for the most part, if you just want to play Grand Theft Auto 6 to enjoy the open world and its story, you don’t need this upgrade. You’ll have a great time with the base game and never think to yourself, “Boy, I wish there were 30 more shirts and a few more cars in this!” GTA 6 is already significant. Don’t worry about making it a bit bigger.

A Vice City mode was using music made by AI.

If you were curious how accurate the utility towers in Grand Theft Auto 6 the answer appears to be: Very.

The best way to play is just to experience the game, even if most of us are too internet-pilled to do that.

People don't like having to scroll a big number back and forth to deposit a specific amount.

It's a funny ad poking fun at another major franchise, but is a bit awkward as Rockstar deals with its own employees trying to form a union.

I could see an HBO TV adaptation of Red Dead Redemption making sense.

#85988. GTA 6 developers at Rockstar are worried about being laid off after shipping "the biggest game of all time"

GTA 6 developers at Rockstar are worried about being laid off after shipping "the biggest game of all time"

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (437 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent.
  • But that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear.
  • "After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent. GTA 6 is already one of the highest-rated games ever - Eurogamer awarded it five stars in our GTA 6 review - and it's expected to be among the most successful, best-selling games ever.

But that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear. Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar North, wrote about their concern for their job and those of their colleagues in an article on The Guardian.

"After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote. "It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

Uriarte's piece comes as Rockstar staff's efforts to establish a union reach a critical point. A tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

Rockstar's UK studios are presently voting on recognising an official Rockstar workers union. Uriarte is in support of it and has urged colleagues to vote in favour of it. Results of that vote are expected today.

"Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that," Uriarte pointed out.

"As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry - one in which workers' voices are taken into account more.".

Across its 12 offices around the world, Rockstar's headcount grew to 4,711 during GTA 6's development - double its size when it released Red Dead Redemption 2.

According to recent reports, as popular and profitable as Rockstar's games are, the organization has initiated layoffs in the past after shipping a major project. While there's no way of knowing whether the same is going to happen for GTA 6, the justifiable concerns - given the current state of the industry - are there. According to the ASGC Games Industry Layoffs Tracker, more than 12,000 developers have lost their jobs this year so far, up from more than 9,000 people last year.

#85987. As a kid, I didn't have a monster in my attic, I had a LAN

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1715 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Pcgamer ↗ Open Full Page

As a kid, I didn't have a monster in my attic, I had a LAN

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1715 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, weird Weekend is our regular Saturday column where we celebrate PC gaming oddities: peculiar games, strange bits of trivia, forgotten history.
  • Multiplayer gaming on PC these days is so easy you probably barely even think about it.
  • Indeed, the best way to play multiplayer PC games back then was via a LAN.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, weird Weekend is our regular Saturday column where we celebrate PC gaming oddities: peculiar games, strange bits of trivia, forgotten history. Pop back every weekend to find out what Jeremy, Josh, Rick and Ted have become obsessed with this time, whether it's the canon height of Thief's Garrett or that time someone in the Vatican pirated Football Manager.

Multiplayer gaming on PC these days is so easy you probably barely even think about it. Most games that support multiplayer will work out of the gate, and there's an abundance of ways to connect and chat with your friends across the globe. This is a far cry from the early days of PC multiplayer, when dial-up connections and ad-hoc servers made multiplayer PC gaming expensive and unreliable.

Indeed, the best way to play multiplayer PC games back then was via a LAN. A local network offered the fastest and most stable connections, and didn't cost you anything beyond the hardware required to hook it all together. Unfortunately, it was also the least convenient way of playing PC games with your friends, as it meant one or several of you had to haul your whole-ass PC to an agreed-upon location.

Because of this, LAN gaming was a rare treat for most people in the '90s and early '00s. Unless, that is, you happened to be a disgustingly lucky bastard like myself, and had a LAN in your attic that you could play at any time.

Now, this sounds like the kind of lie a 10-year-old would blurt out in the playground to impress his friends (specifically, an eight-year-old from the mid '90s who had a working knowledge of PC gaming, which, I concede, is a limited demographic) and indeed, the further away I get from that time, the more like a false memory it seems. But it is 100% true, and I have the pictures to prove it.

The LAN (as it was simply and practically known) was in service between 2001 and 2003, and existed because of my family's long-running enthusiasm for PCs and PC gaming. As I've mentioned in other articles, my dad was fascinated by the internet from 1994 onward, both just as a technology and for the business opportunities it offered. Meanwhile, his brother (my uncle) was an IT support expert and a dedicated PC gamer.

Recent findings suggest that since they were close as siblings and shared this mutual interest (at least on the PC aspect—my dad was never much of a gamer) there was a constant stream of PC hardware flowing through the house, as they tried to keep up with the rapid progress of PCs through the '90s. Eventually, when they'd upgrade a PC, they began taking the old components and building them into a "new" PCs. This is how my brother and I ended with our joint PC in 1997, and how we ended up with individual PCs a few years later.

In 2000 my family (and, separately, my uncle) moved to the Isle of Man, which for non UK audiences is a small island between Britain and Ireland known for two things: tail-less cats and incredibly dangerous motorbike races. The house we rented there had a converted attic—complete with creaky, bare-floorboard stairs—and my dad decided this was the ideal space to set up all three PCs.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Initially the PCs weren't connected. But the layout of the room meant it was only a matter of time before my dad and uncle had that particular brainwave. At some point in 2001, another upgrade happened, and we were left with spare parts for a fourth PC, which could be used as a dedicated server to network the other three PCs together.

The upshot was we had a three-PC LAN on which we could play multiplayer games. I have a distinct memory of them clunking about in the attic while setting this up—likely over a weekend or possibly that year's Easter holiday. I also remember them showing it to us once they were done and explaining how it all worked.

What I don't remember, annoyingly, is what the first game we played on it was. It might have been Doom, though I can't say for certain. I think the reason I don't remember is that once the LAN was set up, my brother and I were largely left to our own devices to get games running on it. Hence, a lot of my memories surrounding the LAN are about that, rather than the games we actually played.

It has been revealed that even with the hard work of setting up the LAN done, getting games to work on it often proved a challenge. Since each PC was the product of multiple rounds of leftovers, they all had different components, so the chance of encountering compatibility problems with a game on at least one of the PCs was not insignificant. The difference between a 1998 PC and a 2001 PC was cavernous, so they might have a processor that was too old, a graphics card that didn't support the latest DirectX, insufficient RAM.

In addition, while we had three PCs, we'd typically only have one copy of any given game, which meant rolling the dice on copy protection with every game we tried (and occasionally searching the murkier corners of the Internet for a crack or a keygen—don't tell the police.) Even if the game installed successfully, there would often be a question of whether it could find the dedicated server on each PC, or whether I'd have to go futzing around in the network settings—not an easy thing to do when you're 13 and stupid.

Nonetheless, there were quite a few games that made it all the way through the gauntlet. The one I remember most vividly is Half-Life: Opposing Force deathmatch—which was basically Half-Life deathmatch with more maps and more weapons. One of OpFor's multiplayer maps, Datacore, was the perfect size for three players, and we'd spend hours setting up laser traps for one another around the map's tight, electric-blue corridors. Another favourite was Paradox Park, which we spent ages in despite the fact it was impractically large for three players.

According to recent reports, pragmatism influenced what we played a lot. While my brother and I never struggled to fill that third chair (weirdly, it isn't hard to get other kids to come around to your house when you have a LAN in your attic), three players was a challenging number with a lot of games, so we tended to play stuff that had a small-scale deathmatch. That noted, we definitely attempted some lopsided rounds of Counter-Strike, each taking it in turns to be the odd one out. Any game with bots, like Unreal Tournament, we considered sacred.

Some of the stuff we played was just weird. There was a Half-Life mod called Firearms, which just had a shitload of guns in it, that we sank hours into. At one point I got super into Operation Flashpoint's map editor, and—influenced by watching Enemy at the Gates—created multiplayer sniper duels where two or three players would play lethal hide and seek in one of its various low-poly towns. When there wasn't a third player available, my brother and I would spend hours hacking each other to bits in Severance: Blade of Darkness' multiplayer duel mode. Did you know that Severance: Blade of Darkness had a multiplayer duel mode? We certainly did, and I think we probably played it more than anybody else.

Industry observers note that looking back, it's wild how hacky the whole experience was. Not the LAN itself—that always worked fine. But how our requirements versus the limitations of what was available affected what we played. Our siloed, odd-numbered setup was perfectly suited for the kind of modern, cooperative gaming experience that did not exist at all back then. But in some ways that was part of the magic. Any new game we got, we'd check the back of the box to see if it had a multiplayer mode and how many players it supported. If we could install and run it on all three PCs and see the host server, holy shit, that was almost as thrilling as playing the game itself.

Industry observers note that the attic LAN lasted until late 2003, when we moved to a different house. I think the LAN was reestablished in the fresh house, but all the PCs were in separate rooms, so it was never quite the same. The physicality of it all was part of the experience, both in the unwieldiness of the hardware and the ability to look over your shoulder and verbally taunt the friend you'd just shot in the head.

In a recent development, even today, when online PC gaming is easier and more accessible than ever, there remains something faintly mystical about a LAN. Players will regularly come together for LAN parties of varying scale, from local and regional parties to massive events like QuakeCon and DreamHack. Given we spend large portions of our lives hunched over a keyboard, PC gamers are a curiously social bunch.

Or maybe we just enjoy killing each other.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you've been having a look around in the Progress section of the GTA 6 Index, you've most likely spotted the Equipment tab. There are 12 unique pieces of Equipment in GTA 6, all of it essential for finding upcoming ways to explore the map and generally being a better criminal.

Sources indicate that while all of the GTA 6 Equipment unlocks progressively throughout the main GTA 6 missions list, if you're feeling a little impatient I'm here to help you understand what's coming later down the line. I'm going to detail what each piece of equipment does in GTA 6, how it can be used, and where it can be unlocked.

The Binoculars in GTA 6 can be used to scope out enemy targets, mark enemies on the map, identify animals from afar, and even let you participate in a little bird watching (there are 60 of them in total across Leonida). The Binoculars can be equipped at all times from your loadout by holding L1/LB and selecting them from there.

According to recent reports, the Flashlight in GTA 6 can be used to help bring a little light to dark buildings and the world itself at night. Admittedly, it's a little cumbersome, so consider going to an Ammu-Nation and fitting a torch to one of your weapons. If you don't want to go that route, then open your loadout with L1/LB, scrolls to where the binoculars are; use left and right on the D-pad on the equipment slot to select the flashlight.

Recent findings suggest that stash bags are essential in GTA 6, letting Jason and Lucia get out from banks and other robbery targets with more than $20,000 in Pocket Cash. Each character can hold up-to two duffel bags at any one time, and any narcotics, jewellery, or marked bills you pick up will automatically be thrown inside. Stash bags have different capacities, which are determined depending on the size of the building you're robbing.

In a recent development, as soon as you're able to free-roam the world in the Gear Up mission, you're free to purchase a pair of headphones. This is entirely optional, but buying headphones in GTA 6 will let you listen to music and podcasts outside of a vehicle. Purchase headphones and earbuds at any electronics store in the world for both Jason and Lucia – just beware: these can be knocked off your head and become lost.

Sources indicate that have you noticed any sealed wooden crates in your travels across Leonida? Well, more often than not they can actually be broken into – often containing ammunition, weapons, collectibles, and more. You'll get the Pry Bar added to your loadout during Chapter 3, where it will equip automatically as soon as Jason or Lucia approach an openable wooden box.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Sources indicate that the Gear Up mission in Chapter 1 is your first opportunity to purchase a mask. These are used to help conceal Jason and Lucia's identities during robberies. While you will unlock a couple throughout the story, you can buy them early or accrue more of them in different styles. You can learn how to buy a mask here, which also has tips on how to equip and fashion them in different ways.

Sources indicate that the Metal Detector is a piece of equipment that you'll need if you want to participate in a side-activity called Underwater Discoveries. Thankfully, this isn't something that you need to purchase. Instead, it'll become a part of your life after you begin doing work for Kenton as part of the main story, and can later be equipped from owned or borrowed boats before you head underwater.

The Slim Jim is a vital piece of equipment. Up until the Moses mission in Chapter 2, the only way you could steal a car was by smashing in its window – a noisy activity which draws attention. The vehicle fence will give you this item for free, allowing you to silently break into cars. It equips automatically whenever you approach a relevant car, and you can learn more about how to use a Slim Jim here.

In a recent development, the Snap Gun isn't available from the beginning of the game, but is well worth pushing into Chapter 3 for. During the Boobie's Time mission, you'll be introduced to a jewellery fence named Yasmani. He'll give you the Snap Gun so that you can help him with a few robberies. Once you've learned how to get the Snap Gun in GTA 6, you'll be able to open locked doors without setting off alarms.

Early on into Chapter 3, you'll have the option to go and meet Brian and Lori. You'll later find yourself down at the docklands, to break into yellow Scoop containers. From that point on, the equipment is yours to keep. You can learn more about how to use the Cut-Off Tool in GTA 6 here, and also find more information on what it can be used to break into later on.

According to recent reports, you'll want to get the Key Cloner in GTA 6 as fast as you can. This handy phone application is what you'll use to break into more modern vehicles, keyless cars that aren't going to be stolen through mere hotwiring alone. It takes a little while to reach the relevant mission in Chapter 3, but I would recommend you push through the story to get here if you want more to do in the world.

It has been revealed that have you tried robbing any Marked Bills without a Dye Pack Jammer? If yes, you've probably had to go home to change your clothes and have a shower to get the pink dye off. The Dye Pack Jammer automatically disables explosive dye packs which are hidden in Marked Bills, which is why learning how to get the Dye Pack Jammer in GTA 6 is essential if you want to rob a bank or payday loans store.

The hunt for World of Warcraft: Forever secrets continue with the discovery of an elusive pet

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (337 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The search for secrets in World of Warcraft: Forever continues ever onwards, with a new breakthrough coming to light in recent days.
  • The cat's name is Ta'Shkal, and they can be found on Mount Hyjal.
  • The way you do so is relatively simple.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The search for secrets in World of Warcraft: Forever continues ever onwards, with a new breakthrough coming to light in recent days. The latest discovery? An elusive new cat that can be tamed by hunters in one of the game's new zones.

The cat's name is Ta'Shkal, and they can be found on Mount Hyjal. An endgame levelling zone, players will have to reach at least level 57 in order to safely make their way up there and recruit this new pet.

The way you do so is relatively simple. You need to find a small corrupted cat figuring within the Felblood Scar region of Mount Hyjal. Once you've found that, you then need to travel up to a hidden lantern south of the Mourning's Rest area. With the figurine in your bags, you'll be able to interact with the lantern, spawning the cat for you to tame (granted you're playing a hunter).

So what's the big deal about this cat? Well, aside from the fact it's got a strange colour scheme of green fur with orange stripes, the cat also has a base attack speed of 1.0. This means it'll attack once every second, which is pretty fast and allows for greater damage output from your pet. This inherently makes the pet valuable for endgame hunter players, who are looking to improve their performance in PvE and PvP.

According to recent reports, this is not the only secret discovered by World of Warcraft: Forever sleuths. Last week, they pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. As of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

In a recent development, the game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among new and returning players. It's the biggest launch in the series' history, and has gone down well with people so far. Even if it has recently suffered its first controversy with a now-fixed gold exploit.

Breaking: GameStop CEO slams 'code-in-a-box' games in the wake of GTA 6's discless release

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (543 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs.
  • Sources indicate that in an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend.
  • Sources indicate that these comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs. Per the CEO, the industry's move away from physical games and towards a digital-only future is harmful to both consumers and businesses.

Sources indicate that in an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend. Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop.".

Sources indicate that these comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch. The game, expected to be the biggest video game launch of all time, is not shipping on discs at all. Even if you purchase a physical copy of the game, what you will actually take home is a 'code in a box' - giving you a code you can redeem on your console of choice that entitles you to a digital version of the game. GTA 6 is not the first game to do this, but it is the most high-profile. Similarly to discs, codes are also region-locked (at least on the PS5), meaning that the proliferation of codes as a format isn't even helping make games more readily available in certain markets.

Sources indicate that cohen notes he's been in conversation with "the obvious [publishers]" but that he's had little sway on their prepares. "Of course they don’t like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying new," he told Bloomberg. "They're taking away competition.".

Recent findings suggest that though Cohen doesn't name GTA 6 specifically in the Bloomberg interview, it's clear that he's talking about Rockstar's megaton launch (he explicitly tweeted "GTA. On a disc. In a case. On your shelf. Like if you still want a physical copy" two days ago). The lack of trade-in potential is clearly harming his business; the Bloomberg article reveals pre-owned and refurbished products make up 22% of the GameStop's sales, down 32 percent from the same time a year ago.

In a recent development, of course, the proliferation of game-in-a-box products doesn't end with GTA 6. Sony intends to stop producing physical discs for upcoming PlayStation games starting in January 2028, moving to a digital-only model despite pushback from consumers and certain developers and publishers. The outcry is doing little to influence Sony's decision, however.

It has been revealed that disc or no disc, GTA 6 is expected to cross $2bn in its opening weekend, and at the moment that is looking like a conservative figure, too. It's estimated the game has sold well over 19.05m units at the time of writing. Despite the astronomical sales, though, employees at Rockstar are still worried about layoffs. Additionally, a tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members (who were fired for apparent breaches of their NDAs) just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

"Let's do with witches what I did with Assassins!": AC pioneer on making 1666: Amsterdam

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1447 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Patrice Désilets is known as the father of Assassin's Creed, but his newest baby is his entire world.
  • Speaking to me at Gamescom, Xbox controller in-hand to show off the Early Access build that had launched that same week, Désilets reflected on the long road to getting Noa's story into players' hands – even if he still expects it to undergo many more changes on the journey to v1.0.
  • Recent findings suggest that we're sharing this full interview transcript exclusively with our members, offering an extra peek into Patrice's approach to development.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Patrice Désilets is known as the father of Assassin's Creed, but his newest baby is his entire world. Panache Digital Games' 1666 Amsterdam finally launched into Early Access in August 2026, the spoils of a hard-won IP battle between Désilets and former employer Ubisoft after he left the studio for the last time in 2013. The timing of its launch seems eerily prescient now that Assassin's Creed Codename Hexe – rumored to be Ubisoft's own witch trials-themed action-adventure – has been reportedly delayed by a year. Having launched into Early Access before Hexe was given a proper reveal, 1666 Amsterdam feels like a bold statement, a flag on the moon of this particular space race: We were here first.

Speaking to me at Gamescom, Xbox controller in-hand to show off the Early Access build that had launched that same week, Désilets reflected on the long road to getting Noa's story into players' hands – even if he still expects it to undergo many more changes on the journey to v1.0.

Recent findings suggest that we're sharing this full interview transcript exclusively with our members, offering an extra peek into Patrice's approach to development. If you'd like to read the whole thing, you can do so simply by signing in, or by registering for free - just enter your email address below.

GamesRadar+: Why don't we first talk about how it feels now to have the game in Early Access after so many years of being in your brain? It must be quite mind-boggling.

Recent findings suggest that patrice Désilets: It's a mixed thing because it's like, "Oh! It's up there!" [gesturing to the game displayed on the TV]. But on Monday we have to continue working on it. But it's great. At the end there's always some doubts – am I crazy for wanting to do this for 15 years? Should I just move on? But it's like no, no, no! Because it's a good thing that I stuck with it even though it changed so much somehow in those 16 years.

If you think about it, it was my first game right after Assassin's Creed, right? So I was really tainted by Ezio and Altair and the ruleset that we'd built over the years. So at first, [1666 Amsterdam] was all about the devil. Like, you played the devil. And I went back to it in 2020, and was like, "I don't want to talk about that anymore. Back to square one again." [I asked myself] What would be the character that represented that devilish side of the world? Like, oh, witches! And I'm not 'the witch guy' at first, right? But I was like, oh, it's perfect. Let's do with witches what I did with Assassins, and let's create an open world and a badass witch using the broom and not the old lady inside a little hut in the woods. So that's how it all started, and now it's out there and people are giving us feedback. The great part is that our goal now is actually to listen and make it better with them.

With magical combat, city sleuthing, and physical roguelike charms, I can't wait for 1666 Amsterdam.

GR+: You mentioned at the hands-on preview that your whole dream behind making Panache was to eventually make a game with the community. So how has the feedback been so far? Like, has it made you think, "okay, now I know what I want to do," even while you're here at Gamescom?

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

According to recent reports, PD: Just like you didn't have a chance to play it yet, I didn't have a chance to actually look at the feedback yet because I'm here talking with people. What I just learned is that my team is excited in Montreal. They're really already in the [mindset of] "okay, yes, there's this and that we can change." They have ideas. And that's kind of how we work – we work in an iterative process, so we listen to the game, listen to ourselves. So it's not about me and my design, saying, "This is what I want, let's do this!".

According to recent reports, there's a lot of things that we tried and ultimately went like, "Ah, you know what, guys, it doesn't work." Like for a while, you didn't play as a cat. Could you imagine? You could possess cats, for a long period of time [in development]. But I was afraid to have a witch and a cat. I was afraid of people going "oh, he's doing cliché stuff there." But like, man, it's a witch! And then what if the cat is the guy from 1999? Because he [the character of Aaron] was just a spectral [humanoid] figure for a long period of time, there to possess people. But what if he's possessing a cat in 1666? And then you'll have the two worlds of 1999 and 1666, two halves woven together all the time, and the relationship between the two characters will make it a whole? And but that's not me being so fucking genius with that, ordering people about. That's not at all how I work. So that's why now [in Early Access], it's just more people telling us, "This is good, this is not that good." We're used to it.

In a recent development, GR+: Talking of changes, I remember last time you mentioned that you lose all Noa's abilities when you die, and that you need to go back and find them all over again in the open world. But it's different now in Early Access?

It has been revealed that PD: Yes, because we are listening! We did some playtests and people were like, "Are you fucking crazy? I spent two hours finding all of this, and you removed them all." So what we do now is that for every coffer and curiosity cabinet you find, you get a new type of ability. Once you find them, you're fine. But when you fail, you just redo a big lottery, so you'll have new abilities and some of them will be the same. But you don't have to find them all over again. So you may approach the mission differently this time because you don't have some of the abilities you had. It messes a bit with your brain, like, "Okay, I had the Warp mechanic. I was good in fights and now I'm less physically powerful, but I'm stronger in Compulsion." So you have to approach the mission differently. And when you finish an Esbat – when you finish like a full moon cycle – then you can lock one or two abilities forever.

GR+: So it really does sound like everything is open to – well, not suggestion, but would you say everything is open to discussion when it comes to the making of the game and how you take on community feedback?

PD: [laughs] Well, eventually there's a limit to the listening! If you don't want a cat but a different animal instead, like, no. You're having a cat. The narrative is our thing. The story – we're writing it, and it'll be a surprise for players. But there's always going to be something cool mechanics-wise that we were never aware of, that the community will come up with.

It's the beauty of making games now. We're in Early Access. Okay, it's not finished, we know. So it's part of the process. But real data comes back, not wishful thinking, and we can actually adjust for real, a little ease of play. Our goal is that we have our backlog of ideas and things we want to do. If the community has the same idea and it aligns, this is priority number one [to implement]. Other than that: we have a initiative.

Jasmine is a Senior Staff Writer at GamesRadar+. Raised in Hong Kong and having graduated with an English Literature degree from Queen Mary, University of London, she started her games journalism career as a freelancer with TheGamer and Tech Radar Gaming before joining GamesRadar+ full-time in 2023. As part of the Features team, her duties include attending game previews and key international conferences such as Gamescom and Digital Dragons in between regular interviews, opinion pieces, and the occasional news or guides stint. In her spare time, you'll likely find Jasmine thinking/talking about Resident Evil, purchasing another book she's unlikely to read, or complaining about the weather.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Matt Damon was clearly trying to fly under the radar during an August 2026 trip to Disneyland to celebrate his daughter Gia’s 18th birthday. Then he ended up clearly visible in the background of internet comedian and content creator Loryn Powell’s video on Instagram, as her daughter was meeting Goofy for the first time. And the video of the movie star dad smiling as he watched and understood how special the father-daughter moment in front of him was unsurprisingly went vital.

Industry observers note that now Matt Damon himself has commented on the unexpected cameo appearance and the story behind it is even lovelier than I could have imagined. During an interview for The Morning Show in Canada, the star of The Odyssey (one of the biggest box office success stories on the 2026 movie schedule) explained how that sweet moment unfolding in front of him reminded him of all the moments he’d shared with his own daughter at Goofy’s Kitchen in the Disneyland Hotel. You can check out what he had to say about it in this Instagram clip:.

A post shared by Loryn Powell (@lorynpowell).

Recent findings suggest that when I first saw the video, I immediately thought, “Now there’s a dad who’s having a flashback of a memory with his own daughter.” So it warmed my heart to hear directly from the Good Will Hunting star that that’s exactly what happened. He, himself, has had that exact moment over the year on annual birthday trips that landed him in that very same spot.

It has been revealed that when we think of Matt Damon, we picture the international film star, the public friendship with Ben Affleck, or even the Damon/Kimmel faux feud that started back in the early 2000s. We tend to forget that he has four daughters, which means countless family events, gatherings, birthdays, and shared experiences, and endless memories from when they were children. It was beyond heartwarming to see his reaction in real time as the father and daughter sharing time with Goofy brought him back to his own family.

Industry observers note that he got called out on all of this in the interview because the host, Brittnee Blair, had recognized a similar look in her own husband watching their four-year-old daughter, knowing how fast time passes and that those moments will merely be memories. Being the movie star on a press tour that he is, the self-proclaimed “anti-Tom Cruise” also related it back to the movies of Christopher Nolan by saying:.

It’s a theme in a lot of Chris’ movies, right? Of a father missing the childhood of their kids. That video, one of my kids sent that to me. We were at Goofy’s Kitchen in Disneyland, and we’ve gone every year for my daughter’s birthday, and she was turning 18… And I had no idea somebody was recording that.

I love when the timing lines up and someone can ask a celebrity to explain the story behind a viral moment, making them more relatable to everyone else. And there’s nothing more human than spending and missing time with our loved ones. I can’t imagine what the family in the video thought when they realized that not only was The Bourne Identity star at Disneyland on the same day, but he was in the background of their video, reacting to that special interaction.

There is no shortage of celebrity sightings at theme parks, from Disney super fan Charlize Theron to John Stamos, Adam Sandler, and so many others. Something like this moment with Matt Damon makes me not only want to keep an even more keen eye out, but also comb through my own videos for anyone making an unexpected cameo appearance in the background. Especially knowing that it could lead to another sweet backstory like this one.

GTA 6 has replaced websites with social media and phone apps because "it didn't feel necessary"

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (470 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.
  • Industry observers note that the web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps.
  • Industry observers note that "It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.

Industry observers note that the web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps. The reason? Smartphone apps just made more sense.

Industry observers note that "It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku. "We definitely wanted to lean into apps and create these apps.".

Though some of the apps in GTA 6 perform similar tasks to the web of old, Nelson remarked the team didn't want players to be distracted from the game's detailed open world by staring at screens. That also extends to getting players to appreciate the value of money, and witnessing the progression of Jason and Lucia as they go from pawnshop robberies to staging major bank heists.

"They don't really need websites to be buying a lot of shit, you know what I mean, and so everything grows very organically," Nelson stated, adding that websites may return in the future.

Recent findings suggest that "I remember asking Stu Petri, our head of 2D and UI, about websites, and he was like, 'For what? What do you need it for?' So, that was it," he added.

In materials supplied by Rockstar ahead of our review, Sam Grosset (associate UI director at the studio) also explained that a lot of thought went into how the apps work, and how easily the phone needed to fit into your play style in order for it to work as effectively as possible.

"We ensure the UI feels like a natural extension of the game world, supporting players without interrupting gameplay or breaking immersion, unless necessary to do so," said Grosset. "The UI should be complementary to the game and appropriate for each scenario. It was a big shift for our phone interface to be in-hand, but it supports that feeling of playing as Jason or Lucia and helps us stay embedded in the world.".

Rockstar would continually "raise the bar, question assumptions, explore newly introduced possibilities, and learn through rigorous testing and iteration" in order to make these apps - and the UX/UI in general - feel in line with the production quality of the rest of the game.

In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, Chris Tapsell awarded the open-world crime game five stars, raving about its absurd level of detail, compelling characters, exciting action and of its big heart.

If you're looking to spend the next several days playing Rockstar's latest hit, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough has detailed guides on everything from individual missions, to core mechanics like the new Wanted Level, and relationship and romance.
